description: CLASP2 Slit-Jaw (Chromospheric LAyer SpectroPolarimeter 2 Slit-Jaw) ultraviolet context imager, the slit-jaw camera of the CLASP2 sounding-rocket spectropolarimeter alongside the Mg II h/k spectrograph, measuring solar chromospheric near-UV intensity images around 280 nm to locate the spectrograph slit and co-register Mg II polarization spectra with solar structure

CLASP2 (Chromospheric LAyer SpectroPolarimeter 2) Spectropolarimeter1 ultraviolet spectropolarimeter channel measuring solar chromospheric Stokes I, Q, U, V profiles near 280 nm, especially Mg II k 279.6 nm, Mg II h 280.4 nm, and Mn I 280.2 nm; one of the CLASP2 sounding-rocket 2019 spectropolarimeter channels alongside Spectropolarimeter2 and the slit-jaw imager

CLASP2 (Chromospheric LAyer SpectroPolarimeter 2) Spectropolarimeter2 sounding-rocket ultraviolet slit spectropolarimeter measuring full-Stokes I,Q,U,V solar chromospheric spectra around 279.4-280.7 nm, targeting Mg II k 279.64 nm, Mg II h 280.35 nm and nearby Mn I blends, with slit-jaw context imaging for coalignment

ChroTel ChroTel (Chromospheric Telescope) ground-based full-disk solar imaging telescope measuring chromospheric and transition-region solar intensity, morphology, and Doppler signatures in Ca II K 393.4 nm, H-alpha 656.3 nm, and He I 1083.0 nm narrowband channels, used for filaments, plages, active regions, and coronal-hole context

EUNIS-06 EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph) sounding-rocket EUV imaging spectrograph measuring spatially resolved solar transition-region and coronal emission lines; 2006 flight long-wavelength channel provided full-Sun/solar-target spectra over ~300–370 Å, alongside the short-wavelength channel covering ~170–205 Å for cross-calibration and plasma diagnostics
instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (2006 flight)

description: EUNIS-2007 LW (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph long-wavelength channel) sounding-rocket normal-incidence EUV imaging spectrograph measuring full-Sun solar transition-region and coronal emission-line spectra in the longwave band, about 300–370 Å, during the 2007 EUNIS flight; counterpart to the EUNIS shortwave channel used for EUV radiometric calibration and line diagnostics
instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (2007 flight)

description: EUNIS-06 EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph) sounding-rocket normal-incidence solar EUV imaging spectrograph measuring spatially resolved coronal and transition-region emission-line spectra; 2006 flight channels comprise the LW longwave band (300-370 Å, including full/trimmed LW solar observations) and the SW shortwave band (170-205 Å) for irradiance and cross-calibration
instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (trimmed/2006 flight)

description: EUNIS 2007 flight EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph) sounding-rocket normal-incidence EUV imaging spectrograph measuring solar transition-region and coronal line radiance spectra; this record is the trimmed full LW (long-wavelength) channel observation in ~300-370 Å, with the contemporaneous SW (short-wavelength) channel covering ~170-205 Å
instrument_name: Full longwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (trimmed/2007 flight)

description: EUNIS 2006 SW (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph short-wavelength) normal-incidence solar EUV imaging spectrograph channel measuring transition-region and coronal emission-line spectra over ~170–205 Å; one of the 2006 EUNIS sounding-rocket channels alongside the LW long-wavelength channel (~300–370 Å)
instrument_name: Shortwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (2006 flight)

description: EUNIS-2007 SW (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph short-wavelength) solar normal-incidence EUV imaging spectrograph channel measuring spatially resolved transition-region and coronal emission-line spectra over ~170-205 Å; the 2007 sounding-rocket flight channel of EUNIS alongside its LW long-wavelength channel (~300-370 Å)
instrument_name: Shortwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (2007 flight)

description: EUNIS-06 SW (short-wavelength) channel of the EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal-Incidence Spectrograph) sounding-rocket normal-incidence spectrograph measuring spatially resolved solar extreme-ultraviolet line radiances and profiles from ~170-205 Å; flown on the 2006 EUNIS solar calibration flight alongside the LW (long-wavelength, ~300-370 Å) channel
instrument_name: Shortwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (trimmed/2006 flight)

description: EUNIS-07 EUNIS (Extreme Ultraviolet Normal Incidence Spectrograph) short-wavelength EUV normal-incidence sounding-rocket spectrograph measuring solar transition-region and coronal emission-line spectra, radiances, Doppler shifts, and morphology in the ~170-205 Å band during the 2007 EUNIS solar calibration flight, complementary to its long-wavelength channel.
instrument_name: Shortwave EUV observation of Sun with EUNIS (trimmed/2007 flight)

description: Evans spectroheliograph solar imaging spectrograph measuring full-disk solar chromospheric intensity in narrow spectral-line passbands, chiefly H-alpha 656.3 nm and Ca II K 393.4 nm spectroheliograms, used for optical patrol of active regions, plages, filaments, flares, and other line-emission/absorption morphology at the Evans Solar Facility

Focusing Optics X-ray Solar Imager FOXSI flight #1 (flight 1, 2012-11-02) sounding-rocket hard-X-ray focusing solar telescope measuring coronal X-ray photons for imaging spectroscopy of active regions, microflares, and flares, using seven grazing-incidence Wolter-I optics modules focused onto silicon strip detectors over ~4–15 keV; launched 2012-11-02

FOXSI-2 (flight 2, 2014-12-11) Focusing Optics X-ray Solar Imager sounding-rocket focusing hard X-ray solar telescope imaging solar coronal, flare, and active-region X-ray emission, spectra, and source morphology with improved sensitivity, using grazing-incidence focusing optics and pixelated semiconductor detectors over roughly 4–20 keV.

FOXSI-3 FOXSI (Focusing Optics X-ray Solar Imager) sounding-rocket grazing-incidence focusing X-ray telescope measuring solar soft/hard X-ray imaging spectroscopy, chiefly ~4–20 keV photons from active regions, microflares, and quiet-Sun sources; flight #3 launched 2018-09-07 with Wolter-I optics and pixellated semiconductor focal-plane detectors.

Focusing Optics X-ray Solar Imager flight #3 PHOENIX (PHoton-counting Energy-resolving Imager for X-rays) photon-counting CMOS focal-plane X-ray imaging spectrometer measuring focused solar X-ray images and spectra (~0.5–10 keV) on the FOXSI-3 sounding-rocket flight of 2018-09-07, complementing the CdTe strip-detector telescopes.
instrument_name: PHOENIX detector on flight #3 of FOXSI

description: GOES-12 (2003–2010) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 12) SXI (Solar X-ray Imager) soft X-ray telescope providing full-disk solar coronal brightness images and flare/active-region morphology measurements in broadband 0.6–6 nm soft X-rays; GOES-M series unit launched in 2001 and used for NOAA solar monitoring in the 2000s alongside standard GOES XRS irradiance sensors

GOES-16 (2017–present) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 16) SUVI (Solar Ultraviolet Imager) normal-incidence extreme-ultraviolet solar telescope on the GOES-R Series platform, observing full-disk solar atmosphere, chromosphere, transition-region, and coronal emission for flare and space-weather monitoring in six passbands: 94, 131, 171, 195, 284, and 304 Å

GOES-17 (2018–2023) GOES-R Series Solar Ultraviolet Imager (SUVI) of Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 17 (GOES-R Series 17; GOES-S/GOES17), full-disk extreme-ultraviolet solar telescope measuring chromospheric and coronal emission in six passbands centered at 94, 131, 171, 195, 284, and 304 Å for flares, active regions, coronal holes, and eruptions; launched in 2018.

GONG (Global Oscillations Network Group) Big Bear ground-based helioseismic imaging spectrometer/telescope measuring full-disk solar photospheric line-of-sight Doppler velocity, line-of-sight magnetic field, and continuum intensity in the Ni I 676.8 nm line; the Big Bear Solar Observatory, California node used with other GONG stations for near-continuous p-mode and synoptic magnetogram observations

GONG (Global Oscillation Network Group) Cerro Tololo ground-based solar telescope station measuring full-disk photospheric Doppler velocity, line-of-sight magnetic field, and continuum intensity in the Ni I 676.8 nm line for helioseismology and solar activity monitoring; Chilean network unit at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory alongside the other GONG sites

GONG (Global Oscillations Network Group) El Teide full-disk solar Doppler imager at Observatorio del Teide, Tenerife, measuring photospheric line-of-sight velocity, continuum/intensity, and line-of-sight magnetic field in the Ni I 6768 Å line for helioseismology, one of the six GONG network stations alongside Big Bear, Mauna Loa, Learmonth, Udaipur, and Cerro Tololo

GONG (Global Oscillations Network Group) Learmonth ground-based full-disk solar Doppler imager and magnetograph at Learmonth Solar Observatory, Western Australia, measuring photospheric line-of-sight velocity, continuum intensity, and line-of-sight magnetic field in the Ni I 676.8 nm line for helioseismology and solar activity monitoring, one of the six GONG network sites.

Global Oscillations Network Group MERGED GONG (Global Oscillations Network Group) ground-based helioseismic imaging network measuring full-disk solar line-of-sight Doppler velocity, magnetic field, and continuum intensity in the Ni I 676.8 nm line; merged products combine six-site GONG observations into near-continuous Dopplergrams and magnetograms

Global Oscillations Network Group Mauna Loa Observatory (MLO) ground-based solar helioseismology station measuring full-disk photospheric Doppler velocity, line-of-sight magnetic field, and continuum intensity in the Ni I 676.8 nm line; one of the GONG network units alongside Big Bear, Learmonth, Udaipur, El Teide, and Cerro Tololo

GONG (Global Oscillation Network Group) Udaipur station ground-based full-disk solar Doppler/magnetograph instrument measuring photospheric line-of-sight velocity, continuum intensity, and line-of-sight magnetic field in the Ni I 676.8 nm line for helioseismology and synoptic solar monitoring, one of the six GONG network sites alongside Big Bear, Mauna Loa, Learmonth, El Teide, and Cerro Tololo

UCAR HAO Historical Eclipse Archive (University Corporation for Atmospheric Research High Altitude Observatory Historical Eclipse Archive) ground-based solar eclipse image archive measuring visible white-light coronal brightness, morphology, and polarization from digitized total-solar-eclipse photographs and expedition records, used for historical corona, streamer, and solar-cycle studies

Hi-C Hi-C (High Resolution Coronal Imager) EUV sounding-rocket telescope measuring fine-scale solar coronal structure and dynamics in a narrow 193 Å (19.3 nm) Fe XII/XXIV bandpass, the original Hi-C flight payload from the 2012 campaign, cited in papers as Hi-C or Hi-C 1 with sub-arcsecond EUV imaging of active-region corona

Hi-C21 Hi-C 2.1 (High Resolution Coronal Imager 2.1) extreme-ultraviolet sounding-rocket telescope measuring high-resolution solar coronal images in the 172 Å Fe IX/X passband (~0.8 MK); 2018 White Sands flight observing sub-arcsecond active-region loops, moss, and fine-scale EUV structure, often compared with SDO/AIA 171 Å data

Hinode EIS (EUV Imaging Spectrometer) slit/slot EUV imaging spectrograph measuring solar transition-region and coronal emission-line intensities, Doppler shifts, line widths, temperatures and densities in two wavelength bands, 170-210 Å and 250-290 Å, using narrow slits and wide slots for rastered spectra and monochromatic images

Hinode SOT (Solar Optical Telescope) diffraction-limited visible solar telescope measuring photospheric and chromospheric intensity, Doppler velocity, and vector magnetic fields; comprising the FG (Filtergraph) with BFI (Broadband Filter Imager) and NFI (Narrowband Filter Imager), plus SP (Spectro-Polarimeter) full-Stokes scans of the Fe I 630.15/630.25 nm lines

Hinode XRT (X-Ray Telescope) grazing-incidence soft-X-ray/Extreme Ultraviolet imager measuring solar coronal emission, morphology, and temperature structure from ≲1 to >10 MK, using broadband analysis filters including Al-mesh, Al-poly, C-poly, Ti-poly, Be-thin, Be-med, Al-med, Al-thick, and Be-thick, plus visible-light/G-band context imaging

IRIS (Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph) ultraviolet slit spectrograph and slit-jaw imager measuring solar chromosphere and transition-region intensities, Doppler shifts, line widths, and images; records spectra in far-ultraviolet bands 1332-1358 and 1389-1407 Å and near-ultraviolet 2783-2834 Å, with slit-jaw channels at 1330, 1400, 2796, and 2832 Å

Improved Solar Observing Optical Network ISOON (Improved Solar Observing Optical Network) ground-based full-disk solar patrol telescope measuring chromospheric H-alpha 656.28 nm line-center and wing filtergrams (commonly ±0.4 and ±0.8 Å), derived Dopplergrams, photospheric continuum/white-light sunspot imagery, and longitudinal magnetic-field products for flare, filament, and active-region monitoring

Kitt Peak Vacuum Tower Telescope (KPVT) 512-channel magnetograph ground-based solar diode-array spectromagnetograph measuring full-disk photospheric line-of-sight magnetic flux density and Doppler velocity in Fe I 8688 Å, with continuum intensity and He I 10830 Å equivalent-width synoptic maps used for coronal-hole and large-scale solar-field studies

Kitt Peak Vacuum Tower Telescope SPMG (Spectromagnetograph) solar scanning spectropolarimeter measuring full-disk photospheric line-of-sight magnetic field, Doppler velocity, and continuum/line intensity, chiefly in Fe I 868.8 nm, with synoptic chromospheric/coronal-hole context from He I 1083.0 nm and Ca II 854.2 nm spectral observations

Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory Ca II K (singly ionized calcium K line) narrowband solar imager measuring full-disk chromospheric intensity at 393.37 nm, used for synoptic observations of plages, active-region evolution, flare brightenings, network emission, and solar disk context alongside Kanzelhöhe H-alpha and white-light patrol data.
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory Hα Film Camera (hydrogen-alpha film camera) full-disk solar patrol imager measuring chromospheric Hα 656.3 nm intensity and morphology of flares, filaments, prominences, plage, and active regions on photographic film, the historical Kanzelhöhe H-alpha synoptic record from Karl-Franzens-Universität Graz.
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory Hα Patrol Instrument (hydrogen-alpha patrol instrument) full-disk narrowband solar chromospheric imager measuring Hα 656.28 nm line-center intensity, typically with ~0.07 nm passband, for high-cadence patrol of flares, filaments, prominences, plages, active regions, and Moreton/EUV-wave chromospheric signatures, commonly cited as KSO Hα filtergrams
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory PDC (Photosphere Digital Camera) ground-based full-disk solar white-light imager measuring photospheric continuum intensity and sunspot/active-region morphology, providing digital photosphere patrol images of the solar disk for flare, sunspot, and active-region context studies.
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory Photoheliograph ground-based full-disk solar imager measuring photospheric and chromospheric solar intensity and activity, producing white-light continuum sunspot images, H-alpha 656.3 nm line-center and wing filtergrams of flares and filaments, and Ca II K 393.4 nm plage/network observations for solar monitoring at Karl-Franzens-Universität Graz
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory Hα (hydrogen-alpha) Pulnix TM-1001 Camera full-disk narrowband solar imager measuring chromospheric intensity and morphology in the Hα 656.28 nm line, used for patrol observations of flares, filaments, plages, prominences, surges, and other solar activity from Kanzelhöhe, Austria
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory Hα (hydrogen-alpha) Pulnix TM-1010 Camera narrowband full-disk solar imager measuring chromospheric intensity at the 656.3 nm Hα line, used for patrol observations of flares, filaments, prominences, sunspot activity, and large-scale solar disk evolution from Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory in Austria
mission_name: Kanzelhöhe Solar Observatory, Karl-Franzens-Universität, Graz, Austria

description: Mees CCD Imaging Spectrograph (charge-coupled-device imaging spectrograph) ground-based solar optical spectrograph at Mees Solar Observatory on Haleakala, Maui, measuring spatially resolved solar spectra, line profiles, continuum intensity, and Doppler/line-shape diagnostics of active regions, flares, sunspots, and prominences, commonly in chromospheric lines such as H-alpha 656.3 nm.
instrument_name: Mees Solar Observatory Imaging Spectrograph on Haleakala, Maui

description: MinXSS-1 X123 SXR (soft X-ray) spectrometer, an Amptek silicon-drift X-ray spectrometer measuring disk-integrated solar soft X-ray spectral irradiance from ~0.5-30 keV with ~0.15 keV resolution, the primary science sensor on Miniature X-Ray Solar Spectrometer CubeSat 1 alongside the XP X-ray photometer and SPS solar position sensor

Mauna Loa Solar Observatory K-Cor (K-Coronagraph) white-light coronagraph measuring linearly polarized K-coronal brightness and derived coronal electron density in the low corona, with full-limb imaging from about 1.05 to 3 solar radii in a red/near-infrared continuum band near 735 nm, widely used for CME and streamer observations.

Mauna Loa Solar Observatory CHP (Chromospheric Helium-I Photometer) solar photometer measuring full-disk and synoptic chromospheric He I 10830 Å absorption/emission, used to track coronal holes, active regions, filaments, prominences, and solar-wind source regions; predecessor/companion context for MLSO He I imaging later cited as CHIP data

Mauna Loa Solar Observatory DPM (Digital Prominence Monitor) H-alpha imaging prominence monitor measuring solar limb and low-coronal chromospheric emission from prominences, filaments, surges, and eruptions in the 656.3 nm line, providing full-disk/limb context images and synoptic prominence morphology for coronal mass ejection studies

Mauna Loa Solar Observatory Mk4 (Mark IV) K-coronameter white-light coronagraph measuring polarized brightness (pB) of the K-corona from Thomson-scattered photospheric light, used to derive low-coronal electron density and track coronal mass ejections over roughly 1.14-2.86 solar radii in broadband visible/near-infrared observations

McMath FTS (Fourier Transform Spectrometer) ground-based solar spectrometer measuring high-resolution solar irradiance/intensity spectra, continuum levels, and photospheric/chromospheric line profiles from the visible through infrared, commonly cited as the McMath-Pierce or Kitt Peak solar FTS, with coverage of roughly 0.3–30 µm (≈33,000–330 cm⁻¹).

MtWilson 60-ft SHG (Spectroheliograph) ground-based solar spectroheliograph measuring full-disk solar chromospheric intensity and activity morphology, chiefly in the Ca II K line at 393.37 nm and also H-alpha 656.28 nm, producing Mt. Wilson 60-foot tower spectroheliograms used for plage, faculae, network, sunspot, and solar-cycle studies

Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania BE-Continuum (Barra Equatoriale Continuum) ground-based solar continuum imager measuring full-disk photospheric white-light intensity near 607 nm, sunspots, pores, and active-region morphology; continuum channel of the Barra Equatoriale suite alongside BE-Halpha and BE-CaIIK.
mission_name: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania, Via S.Sofia 78, 95123 Catania ITALY

description: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania BE-Halpha (Birefringent-filter Hydrogen-alpha) narrowband solar telescope/imager measuring full-disk chromospheric H-alpha line-center intensity at 656.28 nm, used for Catania H-alpha patrol images of filaments, plages, prominences, and flares with a Lyot/birefringent filter bandpass of about 0.25 Å
mission_name: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania, Via S.Sofia 78, 95123 Catania ITALY

description: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania Cook Refractor ground-based optical solar refractor measuring white-light photospheric disk intensity for sunspot and facular morphology, positions, and areas; the historic Cooke telescope is cited in Catania daily solar drawings and photoheliographic sunspot catalogs rather than as a spaceflight instrument.
mission_name: Osservatorio Astrofisico di Catania, Via S.Sofia 78, 95123 Catania ITALY

description: Département d'Astronomie Solaire de l'Observatoire de Paris Meudon Spectroheliograph solar spectroheliograph measuring full-disk solar chromospheric structure and activity in narrowband spectral-line images, chiefly Hα 656.28 nm and Ca II K 393.37 nm, used for plages, filaments, prominences, sunspots, and synoptic solar patrol context
mission_name: Département d'Astronomie Solaire de l'Observatoire de Paris, Paris, France

description: Pic-du-Midi CLIMSO (Christian Latouche IMageur SOlaire) ground-based solar imaging suite measuring full-disk chromospheric emission and off-limb prominences/low corona; comprising L1 H-alpha 656.28 nm full-disk telescope, L2 Ca II K 393.37 nm full-disk telescope, C1 H-alpha coronagraph, and C2 He I 1083.0 nm coronagraph.

Owens Valley Radio Observatory OVSA (Owens Valley Solar Array) ground-based solar radio interferometer measuring solar microwave brightness, spectra, imaging, and polarization over ~1–18 GHz; used for full-Sun and active-region observations of flares, radio bursts, gyrosynchrotron and gyroresonance emission, including Stokes I/V measurements

PROBA-2 LYRA (Large Yield RAdiometer) broadband solar ultraviolet/extreme-ultraviolet radiometer measuring rapid solar irradiance variations and flares in four channels: Lyman-alpha 120-123 nm, Herzberg continuum 190-222 nm, Aluminum 17-80 nm plus soft X-rays <5 nm, and Zirconium 6-20 nm plus soft X-rays <2 nm

PROBA2 SWAP (Sun Watcher using Active Pixel System detector and Image Processing) extreme-ultraviolet solar telescope/imager measuring full-disk and off-limb coronal emission in the 17.4 nm (174 Å, Fe IX/X, ~1 MK) band, used for solar rotation, active regions, eruptions, dimmings, coronal waves, and space-weather context imaging
instrument_name: Sun Watcher using Active pixel system detector and image Processing

description: Parker Solar Probe WISPR (Wide-Field Imager for Solar Probe) white-light coronagraph/heliospheric imager measuring Thomson-scattered visible emission from the K-corona, solar wind, CMEs, streamers, jets, and dust; comprising the WISPR-I inner telescope and WISPR-O outer telescope, spanning ~13.5°-108° solar elongation in a ~490-740 nm band
instrument_name: Wide-Field Imager for Solar Probe Plus

description: Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager RHESSI (Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager) rotating-collimator high-purity germanium imaging spectrometer measuring solar-flare hard X-ray and gamma-ray photons, spectra, images, light curves, continua, and nuclear lines from ~3 keV to ~17 MeV; also cited prelaunch as HESSI (High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager)
instrument_name: Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager
mission_name: Reuven Ramaty High Energy Solar Spectroscopic Imager

description: SATech-01 SUTRI (Solar Upper Transition Region Imager) extreme-ultraviolet solar telescope measuring full-disk upper-transition-region EUV emission in the Ne VII 46.5 nm (465 Å) passband, sensitive to ~0.5 MK plasma, providing solar-disk and low-corona images used for transition-region dynamics, eruptions, coronal holes, and solar activity studies.
instrument_name: The Solar Upper Transition Region Imager

description: Solar Dynamics Observatory AIA (Atmospheric Imaging Assembly) EUV/UV/visible full-disk imaging telescope suite measuring solar atmospheric emission and variability in the corona, transition region, chromosphere, and photosphere; standard channels are 94, 131, 171, 193, 211, 304, and 335 Å EUV, 1600 and 1700 Å UV, and 4500 Å white light.

Solar Dynamics Observatory EVE (Extreme Ultraviolet Variability Experiment) irradiance spectrograph suite measuring full-disk solar soft X-ray, extreme-ultraviolet, and Lyman-alpha spectral irradiance; comprising ESP (EUV SpectroPhotometer), MEGS-A and MEGS-B (Multiple EUV Grating Spectrographs, ~5-37 and 35-105 nm), and MEGS-P photometer at 121.6 nm.

Solar Dynamics Observatory HMI (Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager) full-disk tunable filtergraph measuring photospheric Doppler velocity, continuum intensity, line-of-sight magnetic field, and vector magnetic field from polarized filtergrams in the Fe I 6173 Å line for helioseismology and solar magnetic-field studies.

Solar Flare Telescope SFT (Solar Flare Telescope) T1 Hα (hydrogen-alpha) full-disk narrowband imaging telescope measuring chromospheric solar activity in the 656.28 nm Hα line, recording full-Sun images of flares, filaments, prominences, plages, and active regions; the T1 full-disk sensor of the SFT suite alongside its higher-resolution flare and magnetic-field telescopes

Solar Maximum Mission CP (Coronagraph/Polarimeter) white-light externally occulted coronagraph and polarimeter measuring total and polarized K-coronal brightness, coronal electron density structure, streamers, and coronal mass ejections in the visible corona, chiefly over ~1.5–6 solar radii from Sun center

Solar Orbiter EUI (Extreme Ultraviolet Imager) imaging telescope suite measuring high-cadence solar EUV/UV radiance and morphology of the chromosphere, transition region, and corona; comprising FSI (Full Sun Imager, 17.4 and 30.4 nm), HRI_EUV (High Resolution Imager EUV, 17.4 nm), and HRI_Lyα (High Resolution Imager Lyman-alpha, 121.6 nm)

Solar Orbiter SPICE (Spectral Imaging of the Coronal Environment) extreme-ultraviolet imaging spectrometer measuring solar disk and low-corona line intensities, Doppler shifts, widths, densities, temperatures and elemental abundances; slit-scans the 70.4–79.0 nm and 97.3–104.9 nm bands (including H I, O VI, Ne VIII, Mg IX) to connect solar-wind plasma with coronal source regions
instrument_name: Spectral Imaging of the Coronal Environment

description: Solar Orbiter SoloHI (Solar Orbiter Heliospheric Imager) white-light heliospheric imager measuring Thomson-scattered visible sunlight (~500–850 nm) from solar-wind electrons and dust, imaging coronal mass ejections, shocks, streamers, co-rotating interaction regions, and other density structures over ~5°–45° solar elongation.

SOHO CDS (Coronal Diagnostic Spectrometer) extreme-ultraviolet spectrometer measuring coronal and transition-region emission-line intensities, Doppler shifts, electron temperatures, densities, and abundances; comprising NIS (Normal Incidence Spectrometer) channels at 308-381 Å and 513-633 Å and GIS (Grazing Incidence Spectrometer) bands spanning about 151-785 Å

Solar and Heliospheric Observatory CELIAS (Charge, Element, and Isotope Analysis System) time-of-flight mass spectrometer and extreme-ultraviolet monitor suite measuring solar-wind ion charge states, elemental and isotopic abundances, bulk speed, and suprathermal ions; comprising CTOF (charge time-of-flight), MTOF (mass time-of-flight, including PM Proton Monitor), STOF (suprathermal time-of-flight), and SEM (Solar EUV Monitor, 26-34 nm and 0.1-50 nm flux).
instrument_name: Charge, Element, and Isotope Analysis System

description: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) COSTEP (Comprehensive Suprathermal and Energetic Particle Analyzer) energetic-particle telescope suite measuring suprathermal and solar energetic electrons, protons, helium, and heavier ions in the heliosphere from ~44 keV/nucleon to >50 MeV/nucleon; comprising LION (Low-energy Ion and Electron Instrument) and EPHIN (Electron Proton Helium Instrument) sensors
instrument_name: Comprehensive Suprathermal and Energetic Particle Analyzer

description: SOHO EIT (Extreme ultraviolet Imaging Telescope) normal-incidence EUV imager measuring full-disk solar transition-region and coronal emission in four narrow passbands: 171 Å (Fe IX/X), 195 Å (Fe XII), 284 Å (Fe XV), and 304 Å (He II), used for coronal holes, active regions, CMEs, EUV waves, and solar irradiance context

SOHO ERNE (Energetic and Relativistic Nuclei and Electron experiment) energetic-particle telescope measuring solar energetic electrons, protons, alpha particles, and heavy ions from H to Fe at ~1–500 MeV/nucleon and electrons to ~10 MeV; comprising LED (Low Energy Detector) and HED (High Energy Detector) sensors, often cited as ERNE/LED and ERNE/HED.
instrument_name: Energetic and Relativistic Nuclei and Electron experiment

description: SOHO GOLF (Global Oscillations at Low Frequencies) resonant-scattering spectrophotometer measuring Sun-as-a-star line-of-sight Doppler velocity and intensity fluctuations in the sodium D1/D2 Fraunhofer lines (589.6 and 589.0 nm), used for low-degree helioseismic p modes and candidate low-frequency g modes over roughly 10^-7-10^-2 Hz

SOHO (Solar and Heliospheric Observatory) LASCO (Large Angle and Spectrometric Coronagraph) coronagraph suite measuring white-light and emission-line solar corona, CMEs, streamers, and coronal electron density; comprising C1 spectrometric coronagraph (1.1-3 R☉), C2 white-light coronagraph (1.5-6 R☉), and C3 wide-field white-light coronagraph (3.7-30 R☉)

Solar and Heliospheric Observatory MDI (Michelson Doppler Imager) tunable Michelson filtergraph measuring solar photospheric Doppler velocity, continuum intensity, and line-of-sight magnetic field from the Ni I 6768 Å absorption line, providing full-disk and high-resolution Dopplergrams, magnetograms, and intensity images for helioseismology and photospheric field studies

SOHO SUMER (Solar Ultraviolet Measurements of Emitted Radiation) normal-incidence ultraviolet spectrometer measuring high-resolution solar extreme-ultraviolet and far-ultraviolet emission-line spectra, radiances, Doppler shifts, and line widths over ~465-1610 Å for chromospheric, transition-region, and coronal plasma diagnostics
instrument_name: Solar Ultraviolet Measurements of Emitted Radiation

description: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory SWAN (Solar Wind Anisotropies) ultraviolet all-sky photometer/imager measuring interplanetary H I Lyman-alpha 121.6 nm glow to infer solar-wind proton flux, ionization-rate anisotropies and heliospheric neutral-hydrogen structure; comprising the SU+Z and SU-Z sensor units viewing opposite hemispheres

SOHO UVCS (Ultraviolet Coronagraph Spectrometer) ultraviolet coronagraph spectrometer measuring extended-corona ultraviolet line intensities, profiles, Doppler shifts, and widths from ~1.5–10 solar radii; covers H I Ly-α 1216 Å, Ly-β 1025 Å, O VI 1032/1037 Å, and coronal lines such as Si XII 499/521 Å, with a visible-light channel for polarized K-corona brightness/density

SOHO VIRGO (Variability of Solar Irradiance and Gravity Oscillations) radiometer/photometer helioseismology suite measuring total solar irradiance, spectral irradiance, and disk-integrated solar brightness oscillations; comprising PMO6V and DIARAD active-cavity radiometers, SPM (Sun PhotoMeter) blue/green/red channels at 402/500/862 nm, and LOI (Luminosity Oscillations Imager).
instrument_name: Variability of Solar Irradiance and Gravity Oscillations

mission_name: Synoptic Optical Long-term Investigations of the Sun

mission_name: Synoptic Optical Long-term Investigations of the Sun

instrument_name: Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation

description: STEREO-A S/WAVES (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory/WAVES; SWAVES) radio and plasma wave investigation measuring solar and interplanetary radio burst spectra, interplanetary Langmuir waves, and in situ electric-field wave spectra from 2.5 kHz to 16 MHz; comprising Low Frequency Receiver (LFR), High Frequency Receiver (HFR), Fixed Frequency Receiver (FFR), and Time Domain Sampler (TDS) using three electric monopole antennas for direction finding and burst tracking

STEREO-B IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) instrument suite measuring magnetic-field vectors, solar-wind electrons, suprathermal electrons, and energetic ions/electrons; comprising MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer, ~1 eV–3 keV), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope, ~2–100 keV), SEPT (Solar Electron Proton Telescope), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), and HET (High Energy Telescope) on STEREO-B.

STEREO-B SECCHI (Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation) remote-sensing imager suite measuring EUV solar-disk/coronal emission and white-light corona, CMEs, and heliospheric density structures; comprising EUVI (Extreme Ultraviolet Imager; 171, 195, 284, 304 Å), COR1 (inner coronagraph), COR2 (outer coronagraph), and HI-1/HI-2 (Heliospheric Imagers) from ~1.4 solar radii to large elongations.
instrument_name: Sun Earth Connection Coronal and Heliospheric Investigation

description: STEREO-B WAVES (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory/WAVES) radio and plasma wave suite measuring interplanetary electric-field spectra and waveforms, type II/III solar radio bursts, and plasma-frequency density; comprising LFR (Low Frequency Receiver, ~2.5-160 kHz), HFR (High Frequency Receiver, ~125 kHz-16 MHz), and TDS (Time Domain Sampler) fed by three electric monopole antennas

Sunrise Balloon Flight #1 (June 9-13, 2009) SUNRISE-1 IMaX (Imaging Magnetograph eXperiment) Fabry-Perot imaging spectropolarimeter and vector magnetograph measuring solar photospheric vector magnetic fields, Doppler/line-of-sight velocities, continuum intensity, and Stokes I,Q,U,V profiles in the Fe I 525.02 nm (5250.2 Å) spectral line during the June 2009 Arctic balloon campaign.

Sunrise Balloon Flight #1 (June 9-13, 2009) / SUNRISE-1 SuFI (Sunrise Filter Imager) ultraviolet/blue filtergraph on the 1-m Sunrise solar telescope measuring high-resolution solar photospheric and chromospheric/low-chromospheric intensity structure in five UV passbands between 214 and 397 nm, near 214, 300, 312 nm OH, 388 nm CN, and 397 nm Ca II H, complementing IMaX vector-magnetograph observations

Sunrise Balloon Flight #2 SuFI (Sunrise Filter Imager) ultraviolet/visible solar filter imager measuring high-resolution photospheric and low-chromospheric intensity structure in narrow bands near 214, 300, 312, 388 nm CN, and 397 nm Ca II H; flown on the second Sunrise long-duration balloon campaign, 12-17 June 2013, alongside IMaX.

TRACE (Transition Region and Coronal Explorer) normal-incidence EUV/UV solar imaging telescope measuring high-resolution solar transition-region and coronal emission, morphology, and dynamics in passbands including 171 Å, 195 Å, and 284 Å EUV, 1216 Å Ly-alpha, 1550 Å C IV/continuum, 1600 Å and 1700 Å UV continuum, and white light.

Yohkoh SXT (Soft X-Ray Telescope) grazing-incidence soft-X-ray imaging telescope measuring solar coronal and flare X-ray brightness, morphology, temperature, and emission measure in broadband filter images over ~0.25-4 keV (~3-50 Å), from full-Sun context to high-cadence active-region and flare observations

Yohkoh WBS (Wide Band Spectrometer) solar X-ray and gamma-ray spectrometer suite measuring flare spectra and high-energy light curves from ~2 keV to ~100 MeV; comprising SXS (Soft X-ray Spectrometer, ~2-30 keV), HXS (Hard X-ray Spectrometer, ~20-400 keV), GRS (Gamma-Ray Spectrometer, ~0.2-100 MeV) and RBM (Radiation Belt Monitor, particle/background rates).

ACE (Advanced Composition Explorer) Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris/position data product measuring the ACE spacecraft trajectory rather than particles or fields, providing location and velocity at the Sun-Earth L1 halo orbit in GSE/GSM and related coordinates for time tagging, conjunction checks, and solar-wind propagation studies

Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) MAG (Magnetic Field Instrument) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the three-component interplanetary magnetic field; two boom-mounted sensors, M1 and M2, provide vector fields over ±0.004 to ±65536 nT, with standard averaged vectors, 30 vectors/s snapshot data, and Fast Fourier Transform spectral products for magnetic-field fluctuations.

ACE SWEPAM (Solar Wind Electron, Proton, and Alpha Monitor) dual electrostatic analyzer suite measuring 3-D solar wind electron distributions from 1-900 eV and proton/alpha ion distributions from 0.26-35 keV, providing plasma bulk speed, density, temperature, alpha/proton parameters, and electron heat-flux or pitch-angle distributions with separate electron and ion analyzers.

ACE EPAM (Electron, Proton, and Alpha Monitor) energetic particle telescope suite measuring solar energetic and interplanetary electron and ion intensities, spectra, anisotropies, and composition from ~30 keV electrons and ~50 keV ions to several MeV; comprising LEFS60/LEFS150 (Low Energy Foil Spectrometers), LEMS30/LEMS120 (Low Energy Magnetic Spectrometers), and CA60 (Composition Aperture)

ACE SIS (Solar Isotope Spectrometer) particle telescope measuring isotopic composition, elemental abundances, and energy spectra of energetic ions from He through Zn (Z=2-30) at ~10-100 MeV/nucleon, covering solar energetic particles from flares and shocks, anomalous cosmic rays, and lower-energy galactic cosmic rays below the CRIS range

ACE ULEIS (Ultra-Low Energy Isotope Spectrometer) time-of-flight mass spectrometer measuring suprathermal and solar energetic ion elemental and isotopic composition from He through Ni at ~20 keV/nucleon to 10 MeV/nucleon, with ≤0.3 amu mass resolution and limited ultra-heavy ion measurements above Ni near ~0.5 MeV/nucleon.

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2X MAG (Magnetometer) tilt-compensated three-axis PNI TCM2 magnetometer measuring vector magnetic-field components at 1 s cadence with ~10–50 nT resolution for local substorm activity and ultra-low-frequency oscillations; payload 2X of the second BARREL Antarctic balloon campaign (2013–2014)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation Belt Storm Probes Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Y EPHM (Ephemeris) virtual platform data product measuring time-tagged balloon trajectory positions for payload 2Y of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014), including latitude, longitude, altitude, and geomagnetic coordinates used to locate X-ray measurements from precipitating radiation-belt electrons

BARREL Balloon 2Y XRI (X-ray Instrument) energetic-particle bremsstrahlung X-ray spectrometer measuring precipitating radiation-belt electron losses via 10 keV-10 MeV X-rays; payload 2Y of the second BARREL Antarctic campaign (2013-2014), with 50 ms bands at 10-180, 180-550, 550-840, and 840-1500 keV plus 20 keV-7 MeV spectra

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Y DPU (Data Processing Unit) balloon payload controller/data-system platform acquiring and framing X-ray spectrometer/XRI, magnetometer, GPS, and Engineering Data Interface housekeeping data for Iridium downlink and cutdown control; unit 2Y of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014)

BARREL (Balloon Array for Radiation-belt Relativistic Electron Losses) Balloon 2Y MAG (Magnetometer), a TCM2 tilt-compensated three-axis magnetometer on payload 2Y of the second Antarctic BARREL campaign (2013-2014), measuring local vector magnetic field components at ~1 s cadence with ~10 nT resolution for substorm and ULF magnetic-field context of X-ray precipitation observations

BepiColombo Ephemeris (spacecraft positions) virtual platform product providing BepiColombo spacecraft state vectors—position, velocity, trajectory, and observing geometry for the MPO (Mercury Planetary Orbiter), Mio/MMO (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter), and cruise stack—used to locate fields-and-particles measurements in heliocentric, planetary, and Mercury-centered coordinates

Cluster-Rumba FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) fluxgate magnetometer measuring the three-component DC magnetic field in Earth’s magnetosphere and solar wind; the Rumba/Cluster C1 unit uses dual triaxial boom sensors with selectable ±256 to ±65,500 nT ranges, normal cadence about 20 vectors/s, and burst/MSA high-rate sampling up to 124 vectors/s.

Cluster JSOC (Joint Science Operations Centre) virtual instrument measuring no physical heliospheric quantities, but providing Cluster Model Data for the Cluster-1/Rumba, Cluster-2/Salsa, Cluster-3/Samba, and Cluster-4/Tango constellation: predicted planning data, payload operation plans, spacecraft/instrument commanding context, and model/attitude/operations information used to interpret Cluster observations.

Cluster-Rumba ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument measuring and regulating spacecraft charging by emitting ~6 keV indium ion beams at currents below 50 µA; uses EFW or PEACE potential feedback to hold low positive potential for cold plasma and electric-field measurements and performs ion-current sweeps for charging calibration

Cluster-Rumba CIS (Cluster Ion Spectrometry) energetic ion spectrometer suite measuring spin-resolution 3D ion velocity distributions, moments, and composition; comprising HIA (Hot Ion Analyzer), a high-dynamic-range ion electrostatic analyzer without mass separation (~5 eV/q-32 keV/q), and CODIF (Composition and Distribution Function analyzer), a time-of-flight mass-per-charge sensor for H+, He++, He+, O+ from spacecraft potential/~20 eV/q to 40 keV/q

Cluster-Rumba DWP (Digital Wave Processor) wave-processing and coordination instrument measuring onboard particle-count autocorrelations and supporting WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium) electric and magnetic plasma-wave observations from DC to >100 kHz; one of the five WEC experiments alongside EFW, STAFF, WHISPER, and WBD

Cluster-Rumba EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) active electron-beam drift instrument measuring magnetospheric convection electric field, E×B drift, magnetic-field magnitude, and field gradients by emitting weak 0.5 and 1 keV test-electron beams and timing their one-gyration returns; the Rumba/FM5 unit of the Cluster EDI instruments flown on Rumba, Salsa, Samba, and Tango

Cluster-Rumba EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane DC/AC electric fields, waveforms, spacecraft potential, plasma-density fluctuations, and Langmuir-probe density/temperature; four spherical probes on 50 m booms provide ~100 m baselines, with channels DC-10 Hz/180 Hz/4 kHz/32 kHz, AC 10 Hz-8 kHz, and frequency counter 10-200 kHz

Cluster-Rumba PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) electron electrostatic analyzer suite measuring three-dimensional thermal plasma electron velocity distributions, moments, currents, pitch-angle distributions and spacecraft potential from 0.67 eV to 30 keV; comprising LEEA (low-energy electron analyzer) and HEEA (high-energy electron analyzer) sensors.

Cluster-Rumba RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic-particle imaging spectrometer measuring suprathermal electron, ion, and energetic neutral atom angular distributions; comprising IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer, electrons ~20-400 keV) and IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, ions ~2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon, resolving protons, helium, and carbon-nitrogen-oxygen groups; neutrals ~10-100 keV)

Cluster-Rumba STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) wave magnetometer measuring magnetic field fluctuations in the WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium); comprising STAFF-SC (search coil) triaxial magnetic waveform sensor (0.1-10 Hz normal, to 180 Hz high rate) and STAFF-SA (spectrum analyzer) deriving 3B+2E spectral matrices with EFW (Electric Field and Wave) data over 8 Hz-4 kHz (64 Hz-4 kHz high rate)

Cluster-Rumba WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation) double-sphere active plasma sounder and passive high-frequency wave receiver in the Cluster Wave Experiment Consortium, measuring total local electron density including cold plasma (~0.2-80 cm⁻³) from resonances and natural electric-field emissions over 4-80 kHz using the EFW antenna system

Cluster-C1 WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and frequency-time spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz in Earth’s magnetosphere; part of the WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium), using selectable inputs from EFW (Electric Fields and Waves) electric antennas or STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetic sensors for multi-spacecraft timing

Cluster-Rumba WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz, using one selectable input from the Electric Field and Wave double-probe antennas or Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations search-coil magnetic sensors By/Bz for Cluster interferometric wave studies

Cluster-Salsa FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring the three-component DC magnetic field vector and low-frequency magnetic fluctuations around the Cluster FM6 spacecraft; paired inboard/outboard triaxial fluxgate sensors provide ranges from about ±256 to ±65,500 nT with normal ~20 vectors/s and burst/MSA sampling up to ~124 vectors/s

Cluster-Salsa ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument measuring spacecraft charging and regulating it with an adjustable ~6 keV indium ion beam (<50 µA), using EFW (Electric Fields and Waves) or PEACE (Plasma Electron And Current Experiment) potential estimates to improve cold-plasma distributions and electric-field measurements.

Cluster-Salsa DWP (Digital Wave Processor) wave-processing and WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium) coordination instrument producing timing, compression, and particle-correlation products for wave/particle studies from DC to >100 kHz; one of the five WEC instruments alongside EFW (Electric Field and Wave), STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations), WBD (Wide Band Data), and WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron density by Relaxation).

Cluster-Salsa EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) active electron-beam drift instrument measuring magnetospheric convection electric field, E×B drift velocity, magnetic-field magnitude, and ∇B drift/field-gradient effects; uses coded 0.5 and 1 keV test electron beams emitted and detected after one gyroperiod by two opposing gun-detector units on Cluster FM6 Salsa.

Cluster-Salsa EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane direct-current (DC) and alternating-current (AC) electric fields, waveforms, spacecraft potential and probe-derived plasma density/temperature; four spherical probes on two 100 m tip-to-tip wire booms, covering DC fields to 10 Hz/180 Hz/4 kHz/32 kHz, AC 10 Hz-8 kHz, density fluctuations to 4 kHz and a 10-200 kHz frequency counter

Cluster-Salsa PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) dual electrostatic analyzer measuring 3-D electron velocity distribution functions, density/velocity/temperature moments, pitch-angle distributions, and electron currents over 0.67 eV-30 keV; comprising LEEA (low-energy electron analyzer) and HEEA (high-energy electron analyzer) sensors

Cluster-Salsa RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic particle imaging spectrometer measuring electrons (20-400 keV), ions (2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon; protons, helium, carbon-nitrogen-oxygen groups), and energetic neutral atoms (10-100 keV); comprising IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, three SCENIC [Spectroscopic Camera for Electrons, Neutral and Ion Composition] heads) and IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer)

Cluster-Salsa (SC2) STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetometer and wave spectrum analyzer measuring three-axis AC magnetic and electric field fluctuations and wave spectral matrices in the Cluster WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium), providing B waveforms at 0.1-10 Hz or 0.1-180 Hz and STAFF-SA spectra using 3 magnetic plus 2 EFW (Electric Field and Wave) components from ~8/64 Hz to 4 kHz

Cluster-Salsa WHISPER (Waves of High frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron density by Relaxation) relaxation sounder and high-frequency electric-wave receiver measuring total/cold electron density (~0.2-80 cm^-3) from active plasma resonances and natural emissions at 4-80 kHz; Wave Experiment Consortium sensor alongside EFW (Electric Fields and Waves), STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) and WBD (Wide Band Data)

Cluster-C2 WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic field plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz; part of the WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium), using selectable EFW (Electric Fields and Waves) electric antennas and STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetic sensors for multi-spacecraft timing and VLBI (very long baseline interferometry) studies

Cluster-Salsa WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz in Earth’s magnetosphere; part of the WEC (Wave Experiments Consortium), using EFW (Electric Field and Wave) electric-antenna inputs and STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil inputs for spin-plane By or spin-axis Bz fields

Cluster-Samba FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the direct current vector magnetic field in Earth’s magnetosphere and solar wind; the Cluster C3/Samba unit uses inboard and outboard boom sensors with selectable ranges ±256 to ±65,536 nT, providing spin-resolution to ~20 vectors/s nominal and burst/high-rate data for boundary crossings and shocks

Cluster-Samba ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control ion-emitter instrument measuring spacecraft potential and emitted ion current while reducing positive charging with ~6 keV indium ions up to ~50 µA, improving cold plasma and electric-field measurements by EFW (Electric Field and Wave) and PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment)

Cluster-Samba CIS (Cluster Ion Spectrometry) ion spectrometer suite measuring full three-dimensional ion velocity distributions, moments, and mass-per-charge composition each spin; comprising HIA (Hot Ion Analyzer), covering ~5 eV/q–32 keV/q, and CODIF (Composition and Distribution Function analyzer), resolving H+, He++, He+, and O+ from spacecraft potential/~20 eV/q to 40 keV/q

Cluster-Samba EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-drift beam instrument measuring the convection electric field, cross-field drift, magnetic-field gradient drift, and magnetic-field magnitude by firing coded 0.5 and 1 keV test electron beams from two opposing gun-detector units and detecting their return after one gyroperiod on the Cluster-Samba spacecraft.

Cluster-Samba EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane electric fields, waveforms, spacecraft potential, and probe-derived plasma density/temperature; four spherical probes on two orthogonal wire-boom pairs provide field products from direct current to 10 Hz, 180 Hz, 4 kHz, or 32 kHz, wave fields from 10 Hz–8 kHz, and a 10–200 kHz counter.

Cluster-Samba (SC3) PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) dual electrostatic electron spectrometer measuring 3-D electron velocity distribution functions, moments, pitch-angle distributions, and currents in the magnetosphere and solar wind; comprising LEEA (low-energy electron analyzer) and HEEA (high-energy electron analyzer), covering 0.6 eV-26 keV / ~0.67 eV-30 keV in 92 energy steps

Cluster-Samba RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic particle imaging spectrometer measuring suprathermal/energetic electrons (20-400 keV), ions (2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon; H, He, CNO groups) and energetic neutral atoms (10-100 keV), comprising IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, three SCENIC heads) and IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer)

Cluster-Samba (SC3) STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetometer and spectrum-analyzer wave instrument measuring AC magnetic and electric field fluctuations and electromagnetic wave spectral matrices; comprising STAFF-SC waveform/search-coil data (0.1–10 Hz normal, 0.1–180 Hz burst) and STAFF-SA spectral matrices using three magnetic plus two electric components over 8 Hz–4 kHz

Cluster-Samba (SC3) WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation) active relaxation sounder/passive electric-field wave receiver measuring total/cold electron density (~0.2-80 cm^-3) and high-frequency plasma/electric-field wave spectra from 4-80 kHz, using Electric Field and Wave (EFW) double-sphere antennas in the Cluster Wave Experiment Consortium with STAFF, WBD and DWP.

Cluster-C3 (Samba) WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution plasma-wave electric and magnetic field waveforms/spectra in Earth’s magnetosphere from 25 Hz to 577 kHz, selecting one Electric Fields and Waves (EFW) double-probe channel or one Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations (STAFF) search-coil magnetic component

Cluster-Samba (SC3) WBD (Wide Band Data) wideband plasma-wave receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric/magnetic waveforms and spectra in the magnetosphere, 25 Hz-577 kHz, using selectable EFW (Electric Fields and Waves) antennas or STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetic components; Wave Experiments Consortium with EFW, STAFF, WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing Electron density by Relaxation), and DWP (Digital Wave Processing).

Cluster-Tango FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the direct-current vector magnetic field in the terrestrial magnetosphere and solar wind; the Cluster 4/Tango unit uses inboard and outboard boom sensors, selectable ranges from about ±64/±256 nT to ±65,536 nT, and delivers spin, normal high-resolution (~22 vectors/s) and burst (~67 vectors/s) data.

Cluster-Tango ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument measuring and regulating spacecraft potential by emitting a controlled ~6 keV indium ion beam (<50 µA), with feedback from EFW (Electric Field and Wave) or PEACE (Plasma Electron And Current Experiment) to lower positive charging and enable cold-plasma particle, electric-field, and spacecraft-charging studies

Cluster-Tango/C4 CIS (Cluster Ion Spectrometry) ion spectrometer suite measuring three-dimensional ion distributions, moments, and composition; comprising HIA (Hot Ion Analyzer) for high-flux ions without mass discrimination (~5 eV/q-32 keV/q) and CODIF (Composition and Distribution Function) time-of-flight mass-per-charge analyzer resolving H+, He++, He+, and O+ from spacecraft potential/~25 eV/q to 40 keV/q.

Cluster-Tango DWP (Digital Wave Processor) wave-processing and particle-correlator experiment measuring/deriving synchronized electric and magnetic wave data and particle-count autocorrelations from DC to >100 kHz; one of the WEC (Wave Experiment Consortium) instruments alongside EFW (Electric Fields and Waves), STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations), WBD (Wide Band Data) and WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation).

Cluster-Tango (C4) EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) active electron-beam drift instrument measuring perpendicular electric field/convection drift, magnetic-field magnitude, and magnetic-gradient drift by emitting weak coded test-electron beams (typically 0.5 and 1 keV) from two opposed gun-detector units and detecting their one-gyration returns in the magnetosphere

Cluster-Tango EFW (Electric Field and Waves) long-wire double-probe instrument measuring spin-plane electric fields (0.1-700 V/km; DC to 10 Hz, 180 Hz, 4 kHz or 32 kHz), AC fields (10 Hz-8 kHz; ~3 mV/km-10 V/km), plasma density fluctuations, spacecraft potential, and Langmuir-sweep density/temperature, using four spherical probes on two orthogonal wire-boom dipoles plus a 10-200 kHz frequency counter

Cluster-Tango PEACE (Plasma Electron and Current Experiment) dual electrostatic electron analyzer measuring 3-D electron velocity distributions, moments, currents, spacecraft potential and pitch-angle distributions from 0.67 eV to 30 keV; comprising LEEA (Low Energy Electron Analyzer) and HEEA (High Energy Electron Analyzer).

Cluster-Tango RAPID (Research with Adaptive Particle Imaging Detectors) energetic particle imaging spectrometer measuring 3-D suprathermal electron (20-400 keV), ion (2 keV/nucleon-1.5 MeV/nucleon; protons, helium, carbon-nitrogen-oxygen group) and energetic neutral atom (10-100 keV) distributions; comprising IIMS (Imaging Ion Mass Spectrometer, three SCENIC heads) and IES (Imaging Electron Spectrometer)

Cluster-Tango (C4) STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetometer and wave spectrum analyzer measuring magnetic field fluctuations and electromagnetic wave spectral matrices; comprising STAFF-SC triaxial search-coil waveforms (0.1-10 Hz normal, 0.1-180 Hz high bit rate) and STAFF-SA auto/cross-spectra using 3 B and 2 E components from ~8 Hz to 4 kHz

Cluster-Tango WHISPER (Waves of HIgh frequency and Sounder for Probing of Electron density by Relaxation) active plasma sounder and passive high-frequency wave receiver in the Wave Experiment Consortium measuring total local electron density, including cold plasma, from ~0.2–80 cm^-3 via resonances and natural electric-field emissions/spectra over 4–80 kHz using the Electric Field and Wave double-sphere antennas

Cluster-C4 WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric or magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz, using the Electric Field and Wave (EFW) antennas or Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations (STAFF) search-coil sensors for Cluster multi-spacecraft wave timing and interferometry

Cluster-Tango WBD (Wide Band Data) waveform receiver measuring high-time-resolution electric and magnetic plasma-wave waveforms and spectra in selected bands from 25 Hz to 577 kHz; a Cluster Wave Experiments Consortium instrument using selectable EFW (Electric Field and Wave) electric-antenna inputs and STAFF (Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Field Fluctuations) search-coil magnetic inputs, including spin-plane and spin-axis components

Cassini Ephemeris (Cassini Positions) platform data product providing the Cassini spacecraft position and trajectory versus time, used to locate observations during interplanetary cruise, Jupiter flyby, Saturn orbital tour, Titan and icy-satellite encounters, ring-plane crossings, and magnetospheric passes; not a physical science detector

Cassini MAG (Magnetometer) dual-sensor magnetometer measuring vector magnetic field and absolute field magnitude at Saturn, in the solar wind, and during planetary flybys; comprising the FGM (fluxgate magnetometer) and the VHM/SHM (vector helium magnetometer/scalar helium magnetometer), covering sub-nT fields to tens of thousands of nT

Cluster-Rumba Ephemeris spacecraft position data product providing the Cluster FM5/Rumba observatory location and orbit state vectors versus time in geocentric solar ecliptic (GSE), geocentric solar magnetospheric (GSM), solar magnetic (SM), geographic, and related coordinate systems; contextual auxiliary data, not a plasma or fields sensor.

Cluster-Salsa (FM6, Flight Model 6) Ephemeris spacecraft-position data product providing the Salsa spacecraft position and orbit state vectors for Cluster tetrahedron analyses in geocentric solar ecliptic, geocentric solar magnetospheric, geocentric solar equatorial, geographic/geocentric equatorial, and magnetic coordinate systems

Cluster-Samba Ephemeris (spacecraft orbit/position) platform data product providing time-tagged C3/Samba spacecraft position in geocentric solar ecliptic (GSE), geocentric solar magnetospheric (GSM), geocentric equatorial inertial (GEI), and related coordinates for Cluster Mission science context

Cluster-Tango Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris data product measuring the Cluster 4/Tango spacecraft position and orbit state vectors in geocentric coordinate systems such as GSE, GSM and related mission coordinates; identifies the platform location for contextualizing Cluster field and plasma observations, not a science sensor itself

Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System (C/NOFS) IVM (Ion Velocity Meter) thermal ion analyzer in the CINDI (Coupled Ion-Neutral Dynamics Investigation) suite measuring ion drift vector, ion temperature, density, and major ion composition; comprising IDM (Ion Drift Meter) and RPA (Retarding Potential Analyzer), alongside NWM (Neutral Wind Meter) on C/NOFS.

Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System (C/NOFS) PLP (Planar Langmuir Probe) dual-disk Langmuir probe measuring in situ topside/equatorial ionospheric plasma density, high-time-resolution density fluctuations and irregularities, low-rate background density for ionosphere models, and spacecraft surface potential during scintillation/outage studies

Communication/Navigation Outage Forecasting System VEFI (Vector Electric Field Instrument) multi-sensor electric-field experiment measuring AC/DC ionospheric electric fields, plasma density structure, magnetic field, and optical lightning signatures; comprising three orthogonal 20 m tip-to-tip double-probe electric antennas, a fixed-bias Langmuir probe, a fluxgate magnetometer, and an optical lightning detector

CANOPUS (Canadian Auroral Network for the OPEN Program Unified Study) ASI (All-Sky Imagers) ground-based optical auroral imager array measuring all-sky visible auroral luminosity, morphology, and motion over the Canadian high-latitude ionosphere, often analyzed with CANOPUS magnetometers, riometers, and meridian-scanning photometers in International Solar-Terrestrial Physics/Global Geospace Science studies

CANOPUS BARS (Bistatic Auroral Radar System) coherent VHF radar measuring high-latitude ionospheric field-aligned irregularity backscatter power and Doppler velocity/shift; a 48 MHz bistatic pair at Nipawin, Saskatchewan, and Red Lake, Ontario, using a broad transmit beam and 8 receive fan beams with range gating for 2-D auroral convection maps

CANOPUS MARI (Magnetometer and Riometer Array) ground-based magnetometer/riometer network measuring auroral-zone magnetic perturbations, pulsations, electrojet currents, and ionospheric cosmic-noise absorption; comprising three-component fluxgate magnetometer stations and colocated/broad-beam riometers, typically at 30 MHz, used in ISTP/GGS high-latitude studies

CANOPUS MPA (Meridian Photometer Array) ground-based meridian-scanning photometer array measuring auroral optical emissions and high-latitude ionospheric precipitation along magnetic meridians; four MSPs (meridian scanning photometers) on the ~337° and ~313° magnetic-longitude chains observed filtered auroral lines including Hβ 486.1 nm, OI 557.7/630.0 nm, and blue N2+/N2 bands near 427.8-470.9 nm

CRRES MEA (Medium Electron Sensor) energetic electron spectrometer, Sensor A of the Medium Energy Electron Spectrometer, measuring temporal, spectral, and spin-resolved directional electron fluxes in the radiation belts over ~47 keV to 2.2 MeV, commonly cited as 100–2000 keV, with 17 medium-energy electron channels and a shielded background counter for proton/bremsstrahlung contamination

CSSWE (Colorado Student Space Weather Experiment) REPTile (Relativistic Electron and Proton Telescope integrated little experiment) loaded-disc collimated solid-state particle telescope measuring directional differential fluxes of radiation-belt electrons in E1 0.58-1.63 MeV and E2 1.63-3.8 MeV, and protons in P1 8-18 MeV, P2 18-30 MeV, and P3 30-40 MeV

Dawn Ephemeris (spacecraft positions) platform/trajectory data product providing Dawn spacecraft position and velocity versus time, used to locate the spacecraft relative to Earth, the Sun, Vesta, Ceres, and other solar-system bodies for context of Dawn science observations; not a particle, field, plasma, or imaging instrument

Dynamics Explorer 1 DE-1 (Dynamics Explorer 1) Ephemeris platform trajectory product providing spacecraft position, altitude, latitude/longitude, local time, and magnetic/geomagnetic coordinates for the high-altitude polar orbiter, used to geolocate DE-1 field, plasma, auroral imaging, and wave observations rather than as a science detector

Dynamics Explorer 1 MAG-A (Magnetic Field Observations A) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic fields for magnetosphere-ionosphere-atmosphere coupling, field-aligned currents over the auroral oval and polar cap, and ultra-low-frequency waves; ±6.2e4 nT dynamic range, 25 Hz bandwidth, with ~1.5, 0.25, and 0.02 nT resolution ranges

Dynamics Explorer 1 RIMS (Retarding Ion Mass Spectrometer) retarding potential analyser/mass spectrometer measuring low-energy ion energy spectra, mass-per-charge composition, and flow/spin distributions in the ionosphere, plasmasphere, and magnetosphere; three sensor heads viewed radial, +Z, and -Z directions, resolving ions below 50 eV over 1–40 amu/q

Dynamics Explorer 1 PWI (Plasma Waves Instrument) plasma-wave investigation measuring AC electric fields from 1 Hz to 2 MHz and magnetic fluctuations from 1 Hz to 400 kHz, covering extremely-low-frequency (ELF), very-low-frequency (VLF), and high-frequency (HF) waves such as auroral kilometric radiation, VLF hiss, and electrostatic waves.

Dynamics Explorer 2 Ephemeris spacecraft-position ancillary platform data providing time-tagged DE-2 location along its low-altitude polar orbit in multiple coordinate systems, used to identify spacecraft altitude, latitude/longitude, invariant or magnetic latitude, magnetic local time, and conjunction geometry for DE-2 measurements

Dynamics Explorer 2 MAG-B (Magnetic Field Observations) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic fields for field-aligned current and magnetosphere-ionosphere-atmosphere coupling studies in the auroral oval and polar cap; ±6.2×10^4 nT range, 1.5 nT resolution, ±4 nT accuracy, 25 Hz bandwidth, 16 vectors s^-1 sampling

Dynamics Explorer 2 VEFI (Vector Electric Field Instrument) double-probe antenna electric field instrument measuring ionospheric direct-current and low-frequency electric fields; designed for triaxial ±1 V/m fields at 16 samples/s with ~0.1 mV/m resolution and variational fields from 4-1024 Hz (~1 µV/m-10 mV/m root-mean-square), but flown with the orbit-normal antenna pair undeployed

Dynamics Explorer 2 RPA (Retarding Potential Analyzer) retarding potential analyzer measuring ram ion drift, ion temperature, spacecraft potential, density irregularity spectra, and thermal ion composition (H+, He+, O+, N+ and molecular ions near perigee) from ion flux versus retarding-voltage sweeps (~0 to +32 V), with a wide-aperture duct sensor for total ion concentration irregularities

Dynamics Explorer 2 NACS (Neutral Atmosphere Composition Spectrometer) quadrupole mass spectrometer measuring in situ neutral thermospheric composition and constituent densities from 0-51 amu at 0.2 amu mass steps, including major species such as O, N2, O2, He, and Ar, with baffle scans for zonal and vertical neutral wind signatures in composition variations

Dynamics Explorer 2 FPI (Fabry-Perot Interferometer) high-resolution scanning airglow interferometer measuring thermospheric temperature, meridional wind, and metastable O/O+ emission intensities/densities from Doppler line profiles; observed O I 5577 and 6300 Å, O II 7320 Å, Na 5896 Å, and 5200 Å emissions in limb/horizon altitude scans below the DE-2 orbit

Dynamics Explorer 2 LANG (Langmuir Probe) cylindrical electrostatic probe instrument measuring ionospheric thermal plasma electron temperature, electron or ion density, and spacecraft potential with two independent swept Langmuir sensors, providing continuous in situ plasma parameters and selected high-rate volt-ampere curves at ~0.5 s resolution along low-altitude magnetosphere-ionosphere field-line traversals

Dynamics Explorer 2 IDM (Ion Drift Meter) ion drift instrument measuring thermal ion arrival angles and bulk ionospheric plasma flow perpendicular to the spacecraft velocity, reported as horizontal and vertical ion-drift velocities (±4 km/s, 1/32-s cadence) for convection/electric-field studies; comprising SDS (standard drift sensor) and UDS (universal drift sensor).

Dynamics Explorer 2 WATS (Wind and Temperature Spectrometer) retarding-potential quadrupole mass spectrometer measuring in situ thermospheric neutral wind vector components, neutral kinetic temperature, and concentrations of selected neutral gases, with an ion mode for thermal ion species at altitudes where neutral densities were too low

Dynamics Explorer 1 SAI (Spin-Scan Auroral Imager) visible and VUV (vacuum ultraviolet) spin-scan photometric imager measuring global auroral emissions and geocoronal hydrogen, producing 36°×120° images every ~3–12 min in channels including 3914, 5577, 6300 and 3175 Å plus Ly-α 1216 Å, O I 1304/1356 Å and broad 1370–1700 Å bands

Dynamics Explorer 1 EICS (Energetic Ion Composition Spectrometer) spectrometer measuring energetic ion composition, mass-per-charge, and energy-per-charge in the auroral acceleration region, cusp, and ring current; covers <1 to >150 amu/e in 64 mass channels with 32 energy-per-charge steps from ~0 to 17 keV/e and mass resolution M/ΔM >10 at focus

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series SESS/SSI/ES-3, including DMSP F16 (2003–2020), one ES-3 (Electron Sensor-3) swept Langmuir probe/SSIES-3 (Special Sensor-Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation-3) sensor measuring in-situ ambient ionospheric electron density, electron temperature, and spacecraft potential near the ~840 km polar DMSP orbit, alongside RPA-3 (Retarding Potential Analyzer), IDM-3 (Ion Drift Meter), and SM-3 (Scintillation Meter)

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series SESS/SSJ5, including DMSP F16 (2003–2020): SSJ5 (Special Sensor J/5 precipitating electron and ion electrostatic spectrometer) measuring precipitating auroral electron/ion differential number and energy flux in 19 fixed energy channels from ~30/50 eV to 30 keV; part of SESS (Space Environment Sensor Suite) alongside SSM (Special Sensor Magnetometer) and SSIES (Special Sensor Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation)

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series SESS/SSM-Boom (Space Environment Sensor Suite/Special Sensor Magnetometer-Boom), represented by DMSP F16 (2003–2020), triaxial fluxgate magnetometer for vector geomagnetic perturbations/fluctuations and field-aligned current signatures in low-Earth polar orbit; F16 Block 5D-3 launched 2003, with SESS SSJ/5 (Special Sensor J/5), SSIES (Ions, Electrons & Scintillation), SSUSI (Ultraviolet Spectrographic Imager), and SSULI (Ultraviolet Limb Imager).

DMSP Series SESS/SSI/ES-3, as flown on DMSP F17 (2006–2022), Special Sensor for Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation, version 3, thermal plasma drift/scintillation suite and Langmuir/electron probe measuring in situ ionospheric ion/electron density and temperature, ion composition/mean molecular weight, plasma drift velocity, and electron-density scintillation at DMSP altitude; with Retarding Potential Analyzer, Ion Drift Meter, Langmuir/electron sensor, and scintillation meter

DMSP Series SESS/SSJ5; DMSP F17 (2006–2022), Defense Meteorological Satellite Program Flight 17 Block 5D-3 launched 2006, SSJ5 (Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5) electrostatic spectrometer measuring precipitating electron/ion differential and energy flux in 19 fixed channels from ~30/50 eV to 30 keV; a Space Environment Sensor Suite sensor alongside SSIES and SSM

DMSP Series SESS/SSM-Boom, including DMSP F17 (2006–2022) SSM-Boom (Defense Meteorological Satellite Program Flight 17 Special Sensor Magnetometer boom), a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer in the SESS package measuring vector geomagnetic field fluctuations and auroral/electrodynamic-current perturbations along the F17 polar-orbiting spacecraft track, launched in 2006

DMSP Series SESS/SSI/ES-3 (Special Sensor Ions, Electrons, and Scintillation-3), represented by DMSP F18 (2009–present), Langmuir-probe/plasma-drift suite measuring topside ionospheric electron density and temperature, ion density and temperature, mean ion mass, cross-track and along-track plasma drifts, and scintillation; comprising Langmuir Probe, Retarding Potential Analyzer, Ion Drift Meter, and Scintillation Meter sensors.

DMSP Series DMSP-F18 (2009–present) SESS/SSJ5 (Space Environment Sensor Suite/Special Sensor Precipitating Electron and Ion Spectrometer 5) electrostatic spectrometer measuring precipitating auroral electron and ion differential number and energy fluxes along the spacecraft zenith/nadir look direction in fixed energy channels from ~30/50 eV to 30 keV

Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) Series, F18 (2009–present) SESS/SSM-Boom (Space Environment Sensor Suite/Special Sensor Magnetometer boom) boom-mounted triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic-field fluctuations and perturbations in low-altitude polar orbit for auroral electrodynamics, field-aligned currents, ionospheric currents, and storm/substorm magnetic signatures.

SuperDARN (Super Dual Auroral Radar Network) HF coherent-scatter radar network measuring ionospheric field-aligned irregularity backscatter at ~8-20 MHz to derive line-of-sight plasma drift velocity, echo power, spectral width, convection/electric fields, polar cap potential, and neutral-wind/meteor-trail parameters across high-, polar-, and mid-latitudes

Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) Ephemeris virtual platform instrument providing spacecraft ephemeris, orbit, position, velocity, and attitude state information for locating DSCOVR observations near Sun-Earth L1 and supporting interpretation of its solar-wind and Earth-observing data products

Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the interplanetary magnetic-field vector at L1 with <0.1 nT sensitivity and up to 0.02 s cadence; one of the PlasMag (Plasma Magnetometer) suite sensors alongside the Faraday Cup ion detector and top-hat electron electrostatic analyzer.

Deep Space Climate Observatory DSCOVR (Deep Space Climate Observatory) PlasMag (Plasma-Magnetometer) FC (Faraday Cup) solar wind positive-ion detector measuring 3-D proton/alpha bulk moments—density, velocity, flow direction, temperature and dynamic pressure—at up to 0.5 s cadence near L1; one PlasMag sensor alongside the MAG fluxgate vector magnetometer and ES (Electron Spectrometer) top-hat analyzer

ELFIN A (Electron Losses and Fields Investigation) EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) solid-state particle telescope suite measuring spin-resolved pitch-angle distributions of radiation-belt electrons (~50 keV-5 MeV) and ions/protons (~250 keV-5 MeV); comprising EPD-E/EPDE electron telescope and EPD-I/EPDI ion telescope on the ELFIN-A CubeSat

ELFIN-B (Electron Losses and Fields Investigation B) EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) solid-state energetic-particle telescope suite measuring spin-resolved trapped and precipitating radiation-belt electrons and ions, pitch-angle distributions, spectra, and fluxes; comprising EPDE (Energetic Particle Detector for Electrons, ~50 keV–5 MeV) and EPDI (Energetic Particle Detector for Ions, ~250 keV–5 MeV) on the ELFIN B CubeSat

Equator-S Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris/platform data product giving Equator-S spacecraft position and trajectory in geocentric solar-ecliptic, geocentric solar-magnetospheric, and related coordinate systems for locating magnetic-field, plasma, and wave observations in the near-equatorial magnetosphere

Equator-S EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-beam drift instrument measuring ambient electric fields, magnetic-field gradients, and magnetic-field magnitude by tracking weak <1 μA test-electron beams returning after one gyration; operated at 0.5 and 1.0 keV beam energies with typically ≤100 ms resolution in the equatorial magnetosphere

Equator-S EPI (Energetic Particle Instrument) solid-state energetic-particle telescope array measuring energetic electron and ion intensities and angular distributions; physically part of the Three-dimensional plasma analyzer (3DA), covering electrons at 20-226 keV and ions at 20-400 keV in 6 energy channels and 4 simultaneous angle channels, sampling ~70% of 4π per spacecraft spin

Equator-S ICI (Ion Composition Instrument), also cited as ESIC, energetic ion composition/time-of-flight spectrometer measuring 3D distribution functions and moments of H+, He+, He2+ (He++), and O+; combines retarding-potential, toroidal energy-per-charge, and time-of-flight analysis, covering essentially 0 or ~15 eV/q to 40 keV/q, with 6 s ion moments, closely matching Cluster CIS/CODIF

Equator-S MAM (Magnetic Field Instrument) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic field strength and direction in the equatorial magnetosphere and solar wind; uses outboard and inboard sensors on a short boom to monitor spacecraft fields, with 16-bit data at 128 vectors/s for one sensor or 64 vectors/s for both and selectable ranges from ±250 to ±64000 nT

Equator-S PCD (Potential Control Device) active spacecraft-potential control ion emitter controlling spacecraft charging by emitting variable 6 keV indium ion beams, reducing positive spacecraft potential to a few volts so 3DA and other plasma instruments could measure low-energy particles; beam current could be fixed or feedback-controlled from the 3DA electron spectrum.

Equator-S SFD (Scintillating Fiber Detector) scintillation particle detector measuring energetic radiation-belt/magnetospheric electron and proton fluxes in three shielded integral channels: electrons >0.26, >0.4, and >1.9 MeV, and protons >6.3, >9.5, and >35 MeV, with 64 s time resolution.

FAST (Fast Auroral Snapshot Explorer) Ephemeris spacecraft-position data product providing derived spacecraft location and velocity rather than detector measurements; used to tag FAST auroral particle-and-field observations with geocentric/geographic and magnetic coordinates such as altitude, latitude, longitude, magnetic local time, invariant latitude, and L shell along its polar low-Earth orbit
