FAST MAG (Magnetometer) tri-axial fluxgate and search-coil magnetometer investigation measuring auroral-zone magnetic field vectors and fluctuations; comprising the DC fluxgate magnetometer for fields from DC to 100 Hz and the AC search-coil magnetometer for wave magnetic fields from 10 Hz to 2.5 kHz with high-time-resolution sampling

FAST ESA (Electro-Static Analyzers) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring auroral electron and ion distribution functions, energy spectra, and pitch-angle distributions from ~3 eV to 30 keV over 360° field of view; comprising EESA (Electron Electrostatic Analyzer), IESA (Ion Electrostatic Analyzer), and high-time-resolution SESA (Stepped Electrostatic Analyzer) sensors in four stacks

FAST (Fast Auroral Snapshot Explorer) EFLP (Electric Field and Langmuir Probe Experiment) electric-field and Langmuir-probe instrument measuring vector electric fields from static fields to ~20 kHz (0.1 mV/m-1 V/m), waveforms to 2 MHz, thermal plasma density (1-10^5 cm^-3), temperature, density fluctuations, antenna time delays, and interferometric wavelengths using ten boom sensors on radial and axial booms

FAST TEAMS (Time-of-Flight Energy Angle Mass Spectrograph) mass spectrometer measuring auroral ion 3-D distribution functions, energy/charge, mass/charge, and arrival angles for H+, He++, He+, O+, O2+, NO+ and minor heavy ions from 1.2 eV/e to 12 keV/e; a 360°×8° time-of-flight electrostatic analyzer providing Survey Distribution, High Mass Distribution, Burst, Pole Channel, Monitor Rate, and PHA event data

Kilpisjarvi Geophysical Observatory ASC (All Sky Camera) all-sky optical imager measuring broadband visible auroral luminosity, color morphology, and sky distribution over Kilpisjärvi using fisheye hemispheric imaging; cited as the Kilpisjärvi all-sky camera for contextual auroral forms, arcs, breakup, and optical conjugacy studies.

GOES-10 (1998–2009) GOES-K SEM (Space Environment Monitor) space-weather suite in GOES I-M series (1997–2009), measuring geostationary/magnetospheric energetic electrons and protons, solar soft X-ray flux, and magnetic field; EPS/EP8 (Energetic Particle Sensor; protons 0.8–500 MeV, electrons), HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector; protons >350 MeV, alphas >640 MeV/n), XRS (X-Ray Sensor; 0.5–4 and 1–8 Å), MFS (Magnetic Field Sensor; ±1000 nT vector field)

GOES-10 (1998–2009) MAG (magnetometer), the GOES I-M/GOES-K triaxial fluxgate magnetometer at geostationary orbit, measuring three-axis vector geomagnetic field components (Hp, He, Hn) and field magnitude for space-weather monitoring; primary/redundant boom sensors, ±1000 nT range, ~0.03 nT sensitivity, ~0.512 s sampling; also cited as operating 1997–2009

GOES-11 (2006–2011) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the geomagnetic/geostationary vector magnetic field and magnetospheric variations in three components at geostationary orbit; GOES-L/Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 11 of the GOES I-M series, launched 2000 and operated as GOES-West 2006–2011, with ±1000 nT range, ~0.03 nT digitization, ~1 nT accuracy, and 0.512 s vector cadence after 0.5 Hz filtering

GOES-12 (2003–2010) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring in-situ geomagnetic/vector magnetic field at geostationary/geosynchronous orbit for space-weather monitoring; GOES-M spacecraft of the GOES I-M generation, with primary or redundant boom-mounted sensor, ±1000 nT range, 0.512 s vector sampling, ~0.03 nT quantization, and ~1 nT accuracy.

GOES-6 (1983–1994) EPM (Energetic Particle Monitor) energetic particle instrument measuring geostationary energetic proton, alpha-particle, and >500 keV electron fluxes; first-generation GOES-6 unit with lower-energy detector assemblies: proton P1–P7 (0.8–500 MeV), alpha A1–A6 (4 to >400 MeV), electron (>500 keV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector; >370 MeV protons, >640 MeV/nucleon alphas)

GOES-6 (1983–1994) MAG (Magnetometer) biaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-axis geomagnetic field vectors at geostationary/geosynchronous orbit in Hp (spin-axis/north-south), He (earthward radial), and Hn (eastward) components; GOES-6 unit of the GOES-4–7 spin-stabilized series, with ±400 nT range, 0.1 nT resolution over ±50 nT, and ~0.2 nT sensitivity

GOES-7 (1987–1996) Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 7 EPM (Energetic Particle Monitor), energetic particle monitor measuring geostationary proton, alpha-particle, and electron fluxes in 25 channels: protons in seven bands from 0.8–500 MeV plus HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector) proton channels >370 MeV, alpha particles from 4 to >400 MeV and >640 MeV/nucleon, and electrons >500 keV

GOES-7 (1987–1996) MAG (Magnetic Field Monitor) spinning twin-fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-axis geomagnetic-field components at geostationary orbit: Hp (spin-axis/north-south), He (earthward), and Hn (eastward), with ~0.2 nT sensitivity; after May 1993 only Hp was usable with uncertain absolute level

GOES-8 (1995–2003) EPM (Energetic Particle Monitor) energetic particle instrument measuring geostationary solar energetic and trapped proton, alpha-particle, and electron fluxes, including >2 MeV electrons; comprising the EP8 Telescope, Dome Assembly, and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), with P1–P11 proton channels (~0.8 to >700 MeV) and A1–A8 alpha channels (few to ~1000 MeV/nucleon).

GOES-8 (1995–2003) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 8, GOES-I/M generation) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring three-axis geosynchronous/geostationary geomagnetic-field vectors and magnitude for space-weather monitoring, with ±1000 nT range, ~0.03 nT digitization, ~1 nT accuracy, and 0.512 s per-axis sampling.

GOES-8 (1995–2003) GOES (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites) Ephemeris platform data product reporting spacecraft position and orbit state for time-tagged observations, identifying the GOES-I first-generation Imager/Sounder geostationary spacecraft launched in 1994 and used as GOES-East/GOES-South context rather than a science sensor

GOES-9 (1995–1998) SEM (Space Environment Monitor), GOES-I/M-generation space-weather suite at geostationary orbit measuring magnetic field, solar soft X-ray flux, and energetic particles, comprising MFS (Magnetic Field Sensor, ±1000 nT), XRS (X-Ray Sensor, 0.5–4 and 1–8 Å), EPS/EP8 (Energetic Particle Sensor, protons ~0.8–500 MeV; electrons >0.6, >2, >4 MeV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector, protons >350 MeV; alphas >640 MeV/nucleon)

GOES-9 (1995–1998) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the vector geomagnetic field at geostationary orbit for space-weather monitoring, a Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites I-M/GOES 8-12 generation unit launched in 1995, with three components sampled every 0.512 s, ±1000 nT range, ~0.03 nT digitization, ~1 nT accuracy, and 0.5 Hz low-pass response

GOES-9 (1995–1998) GOES (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites) Ephemeris spacecraft-position platform data product giving geocentric/geographic location and orbital ephemeris for the GOES-9 geostationary weather satellite of the GOES-J/GOES-I–M series, launched in 1995 and identified in heliophysics data as GOES 9 Position.

Galileo Ephemeris platform ephemeris data product reporting the Galileo spacecraft time-tagged position and velocity state vectors for observation geometry, timing, and coordinate transformations during interplanetary cruise and the Jupiter tour; not a science sensor but the mission trajectory/positions context record.

Genesis GIM-GEM (Genesis Plasma Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring solar wind plasma for sample-collector state selection and science distributions, comprising GIM (Genesis Ion Monitor) ion E/q analyzer covering ~100 eV-14 keV and GEM (Genesis Electron Monitor) electron analyzer covering 1-1400 eV at L1

Geotail CPI (Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation) quadrispherical analyzer suite measuring 3-D electron and positive-ion velocity distributions and ion composition; comprising the HP (Hot Plasma) analyzer for electrons and ions at 1-50,000 eV/q, the SW (Solar Wind) ion analyzer at 150-7,000 eV/q, and the IC (Ion Composition) analyzer covering ~1-550 u/q at 100 eV and ~1-55 u/q at 10 keV

Geotail MGF (Magnetic Field Experiment) magnetometer suite measuring vector magnetic fields and low-frequency magnetic fluctuations in the magnetotail, magnetosphere, and solar wind; comprising dual three-axis fluxgate magnetometers (FGM, ±16 to ±65536 nT ranges, 16 vectors/s) and a three-axis search-coil magnetometer (SCM, ~0.5–50 Hz class fluctuations)

Geotail Ephemeris (spacecraft position) platform data product giving Geotail spacecraft location and trajectory relative to Earth for contextualizing plasma, field, and particle observations, with position vectors in common geocentric coordinate systems such as GSE, GSM, GEI, and SM rather than a science sensor measurement.

Geotail LEP (Low Energy Particle Experiment) quadrispherical electrostatic analyzer suite measuring low-energy plasma and energetic ions/electrons in the magnetotail and solar wind; comprising LEP-EA (Energy-per-charge Analyzer) with EA-e and EA-i electron/ion analyzers for 3-D distributions from several eV/q to 43 keV/q, LEP-SW (Solar Wind ion analyzer), and LEP-MS (energetic-ion Mass Spectrometer, failed shortly after launch)

Geotail SWA (Solar Wind Analyzer) quadrispherical electrostatic plasma analyzer measuring three-dimensional solar-wind ion fluxes, velocity distributions, and moments over 150-7,000 eV/q; a sensor of the CPI (Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation) suite alongside the HPA (Hot Plasma Analyzer) for hot magnetospheric plasma

Geotail HPA (Hot Plasma Analyzer) quadrispherical electrostatic plasma analyzer of the CPI (Comprehensive Plasma Instrumentation) suite measuring three-dimensional electron and ion differential fluxes, velocity distributions, densities, temperatures, and flows over ~1-50,000 eV/q in the terrestrial magnetosphere and solar wind

Geotail EPIC (Energetic Particles and Ion Composition) quadrispherical analyzer particle composition suite measuring suprathermal and energetic ion charge state, mass, energy and angular distributions plus energetic electrons; comprising STICS (Supra-Thermal Ion Composition Spectrometer, 10-230 keV/q ions) and ICS (Ion Composition Subsystem, <50 keV-3 MeV ions and >30 keV electrons)

Geotail PWI (Plasma Wave Investigation) plasma wave receiver suite measuring electric and magnetic field spectra and waveforms in the magnetotail; comprising SFA (Sweep Frequency Analyzer), MCA (Multi-Channel Analyzer) and WFC (Wave-Form Capture), using WANT wire and PANT probe 100 m tip-to-tip electric dipoles plus triaxial search coils, with E-field 5.6 Hz-800 kHz, B-field 5.6 Hz-12.5 kHz and WFC 10 Hz-4 kHz

Giotto Ephemeris (Giotto Positions) platform ephemeris data product providing the Giotto spacecraft trajectory, position, and timing context in heliocentric/geocentric coordinates for interpreting in situ plasma, fields, dust, and neutral-gas measurements during the ESA Halley-comet flyby mission

GOES-10 (1998–2009) Ephemeris platform position data product for the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 10 spacecraft, providing spacecraft geocentric/geostationary location, orbital longitude, orbit information, and time-tagged position vectors as ancillary context rather than a particle, field, or photon science sensor.

GOES-11 (2006–2011; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 11, prelaunch GOES-L) Ephemeris platform data product providing spacecraft position and orbit information for the GOES I-M geostationary fleet/GOES mission, launched in 2000 and used for heliophysics context as a geocentric/geostationary observing location, including longitude, radius, and time-tagged orbital position rather than particle or field measurements

GOES-11 (2006–2011) SEM (Space Environment Monitor) space-weather instrument suite measuring geosynchronous magnetic fields, solar soft X-ray flux, and energetic particle fluxes; comprising MFS (Magnetic Field Sensor, ±1000 nT), XRS (Solar X-ray Sensor, 0.5–5 Å and 1–8 Å), EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor, protons 0.8–500 MeV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector, protons >350 MeV and alpha particles >640 MeV/nucleon)

GOES-12 (2003–2010) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 12) Ephemeris spacecraft-position platform data providing geostationary satellite location for heliophysics context, identifying the GOES-M flight unit used as GOES-East and later GOES-South America during the 2001–2013 GOES I–M era rather than an in situ particle or field sensor

GOES-13 (2010–2017) EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor), energetic particle monitor on the GOES-N/GOES-13 spacecraft launched 2006 for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites, measuring geosynchronous electrons, protons, and alpha particles; comprises MAGED (Magnetospheric Electron Detector), MAGPD (Magnetospheric Proton Detector), EPEAD (Energetic Proton, Electron, and Alpha Detector), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), covering e− 30 keV->4 MeV, p+ 80 keV->700 MeV, α 3.8->3400 MeV

GOES-13 (2010–2017) Ephemeris spacecraft platform data product providing position and orbit/geostationary trajectory information for heliophysics context, including time-tagged geocentric location, longitude/latitude/altitude or Cartesian coordinates used to place GOES-13 particle, X-ray, EUV, and magnetic-field observations in space and time

GOES-13 (2010–2017) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring local geostationary geomagnetic-field magnitude, vector components, field vector, and magnetic-field variations for sudden impulses, magnetopause crossings, and geomagnetic activity; GOES-N/O/P generation unit GOES-13/GOES-N, launched 2006 and used as GOES-East 2010–2017, with primary and backup boom-mounted sensors.

GOES-13 (2010–2017) SEM (Space Environment Monitor) suite, GOES-N series/GOES-East 2010–2017, measuring geostationary space weather: solar soft X-ray irradiance/flux with XRS (X-Ray Sensor) 0.05–0.3 and 0.1–0.8 nm bands, solar EUV flux with EUVS (Extreme Ultraviolet Sensor) ~10–126 nm, energetic electrons/protons/alpha particles with EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor) and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), and geomagnetic/local vector magnetic field with MAG (Magnetometer)

GOES-14 (2009–2020) EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor) energetic-particle monitor on the GOES-O/GOES-NOP series, launched in 2009, measuring geosynchronous electrons, protons, and alpha particles; includes MAGED (Magnetospheric Electron Detector), MAGPD (Magnetospheric Proton Detector), EPEAD (Energetic Proton, Electron, and Alpha Detector), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector); ranges: electrons ~30 keV–>4 MeV, protons ~80 keV–>700 MeV, alphas ~3.8–>3400 MeV

GOES-14 (2009–2020) ephemeris platform-position data product for the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 14 geostationary unit, launched as GOES-O, providing spacecraft position, orbit, state/trajectory context, geocentric position and velocity, altitude, latitude/longitude or sub-satellite longitude, and time tags for use with GOES space-weather measurements

GOES-14 (2009–2020) (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 14) MAG (Magnetometer) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector geomagnetic field magnitude/strength and direction near geostationary orbit, with outboard and inboard boom sensors monitoring magnetic variations, sudden impulses, solar-wind shock signatures, and geomagnetic activity.

GOES-14 (2009–2020) SEM (Space Environment Monitor) measuring geomagnetic field vectors, solar X-ray flux/UV irradiance, and energetic electron/proton/alpha fluxes; with MAG magnetometer, XRS (X-Ray Sensor; 0.05–0.4/0.1–0.8 nm), EUVS (Extreme Ultraviolet Sensor; five ~5–127 nm bands), and EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor: MAGED/MAGPD Magnetospheric Electron/Proton Detectors, EPEAD Energetic Proton Electron and Alpha Detector, HEPAD High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector; ~30 keV–>700 MeV)

GOES-15 (2010–2020) EPS (Energetic Particle Sensor) energetic particle monitor at geostationary/geosynchronous orbit measuring trapped and solar protons, electrons, and alpha particles; comprising MAGED (Magnetospheric Electron Detector), MAGPD (Magnetospheric Proton Detector), EPEAD (Energetic Proton, Electron, and Alpha Detector), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector), covering electrons 30 keV–4 MeV, protons 80 keV–700 MeV, alphas 3.8–3400 MeV

GOES-15 (2010–2020) Ephemeris for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites 15, a spacecraft/platform position data product providing time-tagged location, orbital position/longitude, geocentric coordinates, and attitude for the GOES-15 geostationary spacecraft, used to place GOES-15 particle, X-ray, EUV, and magnetic-field observations in heliophysics analyses

GOES-15 (2010–2020) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the local vector geomagnetic field and magnetic field variations at geosynchronous orbit for the GOES-N/O/P generation; GOES-15 is the GOES-P spacecraft, with inboard and outboard boom-mounted fluxgate sensors providing Hp, He, and Hn components for sudden impulses, magnetic storms, and magnetospheric field variations

GOES-15 (2010–2020)/Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite 15 SEM/Space Environment Monitor: geosynchronous energetic e−/p+/α particles, solar soft X-ray/EUV flux, geomag vector field; EPS/Energetic Particle Sensor (EPEAD/Energetic Proton Electron & Alpha Detector;MAGED/Magnetospheric Electron Detector;MAGPD/Magnetospheric Proton Detector;HEPAD/High Energy Proton & Alpha Detector); XRS/X-Ray Sensor (0.05–0.4/0.1–0.8 nm); EUVS/Extreme Ultraviolet Sensor (~10–126 nm); MAG/magnetometer

GOES-16 (2017–present) GOES (Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites) Ephemeris platform/orbit data product providing spacecraft position, orbit, and geostationary location information, with time-tagged GOES-16 position vectors/coordinates for locating and interpreting GOES-R series space-weather observations rather than a particle, field, or photon sensor.

GOES-17 (2018–2023) Ephemeris spacecraft position/platform data product providing GOES-17 Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite location, orbit, velocity, and geocentric/geographic coordinates for observation geometry and field-line context; GOES-R series unit launched as GOES-S in 2018 and operated as GOES-West near 137.2°W during 2019–2023

GOLD GOLD (Global-scale Observations of the Limb and Disk) two-channel far-ultraviolet imaging spectrograph measuring Earth thermosphere-ionosphere airglow from geostationary orbit; comprising redundant Channel A and Channel B sensors covering ~132-162 nm, including OI 135.6 nm and N2 Lyman-Birge-Hopfield bands for O/N2, neutral temperature, and nighttime ionospheric density

International GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) Service (IGS) GPS (Global Positioning System) receiver ground-based radio waveform receiver measuring dual-frequency L-band GNSS code, carrier phase, Doppler, and signal strength observables (notably GPS L1 1575.42 MHz and L2 1227.60 MHz) for precise orbits, clocks, station positions, and ionospheric total electron content.

Helios 1 E3 (Fluxgate Magnetometer for Average Fields) boom-mounted triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the interplanetary magnetic-field vector and average-field variations in the inner heliosphere, with autoranged ±16, ±48, ±144, and ±432 nT ranges and vector sampling up to 1-16 s⁻¹ depending on telemetry bit rate

Helios E3 (Fluxgate Magnetometer for Average Fields) boom-mounted triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the interplanetary magnetic-field vector and onboard averages/variances in the inner heliosphere; automatic ranges ±16, ±48, ±144 and ±432 nT, with vector sampling up to 1-16 s^-1 depending on telemetry.

Helios 1 E1 (Plasma Experiment) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring solar-wind ion and electron velocity distribution functions and derived plasma moments; comprising ion sensors I1a, I1b, and I3 for protons and heavier positive ions at 0.155-15.32 keV/e, and electron sensor I2 for 0.5-1660 eV electrons with one-dimensional angular resolution

Helios 1 E6 (Cosmic Ray Particles) energetic-particle telescope measuring solar, planetary and galactic cosmic-ray ions and electrons in interplanetary space (0.3-1 AU): protons and alpha particles >1.3 MeV/nucleon in six channels (1.3-3.3, 3.3-13, 13-27, 27-37, 37-45, >45 MeV/nucleon) and electrons >0.3 MeV in five channels (0.3-0.8, 0.8-2, 2-3, 3-4, >4 MeV)

Helios 1 Ephemeris spacecraft position/trajectory data product providing the Helios 1 spacecraft location and velocity for contextualizing in situ solar-wind, magnetic-field, plasma, and energetic-particle measurements, typically in heliocentric and geocentric coordinate systems rather than a physical detector measurement.

Helios 2 E1 (Plasma Experiment) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring solar wind electron, proton, and heavy-ion velocity distribution functions and derived bulk plasma parameters; comprising ion analyzers I1a, I1b, and I3 for positive particles at 0.155-15.32 keV/q and electron analyzer I2 for 0.5-1660 eV electrons with one-dimensional angular resolution

Helios E6 (Cosmic Ray Particles) energetic particle telescope measuring high-energy charged particles of solar, planetary, and galactic origin from 0.3-1 AU; proton and alpha channels at 1.3-3.3, 3.3-13, 13-27, 27-37, 37-45, and >45 MeV/nucleon, and electron channels at 0.3-0.8, 0.8-2, 2-3, 3-4, and >4 MeV, with a 55° field of view

Helios 2 Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris/position data product providing the Helios 2 trajectory and location vectors in standard heliocentric and geocentric coordinate systems, used to contextualize in-situ solar-wind plasma, magnetic-field, radio-wave, and energetic-particle observations in the inner heliosphere

Hawkeye MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the ambient vector magnetic field in Earth’s magnetosphere and solar wind, with sequential three-axis samples every 5.72 s, four commandable ranges of ±150, ±450, ±1500, and ±25,000 nT, and frequency response flat from dc to 1 Hz and down 3 dB at 10 Hz.

Hawkeye VLF (Very Low Frequency) long-wire electric-field and search-coil wave instrument measuring dc electric fields and low-frequency plasma waves; electric spectra in 16 logarithmic channels from 1.78 Hz to 178 kHz, magnetic spectra in 8 channels from 1.78 Hz to 5.62 kHz, with wideband receiver ranges of 0.15-10 kHz or 1-45 kHz sampled every 11.52 s

ISIS-1 (International Satellites for Ionospheric Studies 1) SFS (Swept-Frequency Sounder) topside ionosonde/radio sounder measuring ionospheric electron density and virtual range from ~300-3500 km by transmitted-pulse echoes; swept 0.1-20 MHz every 19 or 29 s, with fixed-frequency and mixed modes at six selected frequencies, producing ionograms with plasma resonances and ground echoes

ISIS 2 SFS (Swept-Frequency Sounder) topside ionosonde measuring ionospheric electron-density profiles and plasma structure at ~300-1400 km by radio-pulse sounding from 0.1 to 20 MHz every 14 or 21 s; operated in swept-frequency, six-frequency fixed-sound, and mixed fixed-transmit/swept-receive modes, producing ionograms with virtual-range echoes and plasma resonances.

IMP 8 (Interplanetary Monitoring Platform 8) MAG (Magnetic Field Experiment) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector interplanetary magnetic field components and magnitude near Earth’s solar-wind environment, with original full-scale ranges of ±12, ±36, and ±108 nT and subsequent fixed ±36 nT operation at ~320 ms vector cadence

IMP spacecraft series MCGUIRE (McGuire/Goddard Space Flight Center Solar and Cosmic-Ray Particles experiment) energetic particle instrument measuring solar and galactic electrons, protons, and heavy ions to Z=30, with integral electron channels >150, >350, >700 keV, proton thresholds 0.05-25 MeV, Z=1-16 ions at 4-20 MeV/nucleon, and 2-12 MeV electrons plus Z=1-30 nuclei at 20-500 MeV/nucleon with sector anisotropies

IMP 8 PLS (Plasma Science) modulated split-collector Faraday-cup plasma analyzer measuring solar-wind, transition-region, and magnetotail positive ion and electron directional spectra; ions are sampled in 24 energy/charge windows from 50–7000 V and electrons in 21 windows from 23–1935 V, yielding routine proton bulk speed, density, and temperature from Maxwellian fits

IMP 8 (Interplanetary Monitoring Platform 8, Explorer 50/IMP-J) spacecraft ephemeris data product providing spacecraft position and trajectory in geocentric and solar-terrestrial coordinate systems, used to locate IMP 8 plasma, magnetic-field, and energetic-particle measurements in the solar wind, magnetosheath, and distant magnetosphere

Interball-2 SKA-3 (Electron and proton distribution) energetic particle spectrometer set measuring electron and ion distribution functions; comprising EA-2 electron and EA-3 ion energy-angle analyzers at 30, 85, 240, 680, 1900, 5300, 15000 eV in eight sectors, plus oppositely directed EM-1-1 and EM-1-2 time-of-flight energy-mass spectrometers for electrons and H+, He+, O+ ions from ~20-500 keV

Interball-2 DOK-2A (Electron and Proton Anisotropy) energetic particle telescope measuring auroral/magnetospheric electron and proton fluxes, spectra, and pitch-angle anisotropy; four silicon telescopes 1e/2e for electrons (20-420 keV) and 1p/2p for ions/protons (20-850 keV), with a fixed antisolar pair and a mechanically scanning pair for 3-D distributions over each spin

Interball-2 PROMICS-3 (PROGNOZ Magnetospheric Ion Composition Spectrometer) electrostatic analyzer suite measuring 3-D ion distributions with mass separation M=1–32 from 4 eV to 70 keV and electron distributions from 12 eV to 35 keV; comprising MEPS (magnetospheric electron plasma spectrometer) and TRICS (three-dimensional ion composition spectrometer) sensors

Interball-2 IMAP-3 (Three-Axis Magnetic Field) magnetometer measuring the three-component DC magnetic field in the auroral magnetosphere, for inner-magnetosphere structure and small-scale field-aligned currents; ranges ±6800 nT at 1 nT resolution and ±68000 nT at 10 nT resolution, with 3 s standard vectors and 2 or 8 vectors/s burst data

Interball-2 Ephemeris (spacecraft orbit) platform data product measuring time-tagged spacecraft position and velocity, geocentric distance, altitude, and magnetospheric location context for the Interball-2 Auroral Probe, used to relate fields and plasma observations to Earth, the bow shock, magnetopause, magnetotail, and auroral regions

IBEX Hi (high-energy energetic neutral atom camera) neutral atom imager measuring energetic neutral atoms (ENAs) from the outer heliosphere in six energy bands, band 1-6: 0.38-0.59, 0.52-0.95, 0.84-1.55, 1.36-2.50, 1.99-3.75, and 3.13-6.00 keV, complementing the IBEX Lo sensor for lower-energy ENA sky maps

IBEX Ephemeris (Interstellar Boundary Explorer spacecraft ephemeris) virtual platform instrument providing spacecraft position, velocity, geocentric 8-day orbit context (~7000 km perigee to ~37 RE apogee), Sun-pointed spin-axis attitude, and timing/pointing needed to interpret IBEX-Lo and IBEX-Hi energetic neutral atom sky maps

IBEX-Lo (Interstellar Boundary Explorer Low Energy) neutral atom imager measuring low-energy energetic neutral atom (ENA) sky maps, composition, and angular fluxes from ~0.01-2.0 keV; a single-pixel imager with 7°×7° and high-resolution 3.5°×3.5° fields of view, bands 1-8 centered at 14, 27, 52, 102, 197, 451, 908, and 1903 eV, and triple-coincidence time-of-flight mass analysis for H, O, and He ENAs

Ionospheric Connection Explorer MIGHTI (Michelson Interferometer for Global High-resolution Thermospheric Imaging) limb-viewing Doppler interferometer measuring thermospheric neutral line-of-sight and vector winds and temperatures from airglow; comprising MIGHTI-A and MIGHTI-B units viewing 90° apart, with green 557.7 nm OI and red 630.0 nm OI channels over roughly 90–300 km altitude

Ionospheric Connection Explorer FUV (Far Ultra-Violet Imaging Spectrograph) limb-imaging ultraviolet spectrograph measuring terrestrial airglow in ~115-180 nm, especially OI 135.6 nm and N2 Lyman-Birge-Hopfield bands, to retrieve nighttime ionospheric electron density and daytime thermospheric composition along the magnetic meridian.

Ionospheric Connection Explorer EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Spectrograph) one-dimensional push-broom imaging spectrograph measuring daytime ionospheric extreme-ultraviolet airglow, especially O II 83.4 nm and 61.7 nm emissions, to retrieve vertical profiles and global morphology of thermospheric/ionospheric O+ density along the limb/sky wedge

Ionospheric Connection Explorer IVM (Ion Velocity Meter) planar thermal-ion drift instrument measuring in situ F-region ion velocity/drift vector, ram speed, plasma density, ion temperature and composition; comprising an RPA (retarding potential analyzer) for ram energy analysis and an IDM (ion drift meter) for cross-track ion arrival angles/drifts

Thule Air Base Geophysical Observatory TAB (Thule Air Base) Magnetometer ground-based magnetometer measuring the local geomagnetic-field vector and time variations at the high-latitude polar-cap station in northwest Greenland, for studies of auroral electrojets, ionospheric currents, magnetic pulsations, substorms, and solar-wind/magnetosphere coupling

IAGA (International Association of Geomagnetism and Aeronomy) VOS (Vostok) station magnetometer measuring ground geomagnetic field vector and temporal variations at Vostok Antarctic observatory, reported as observatory components such as H, D, Z or X, Y, Z and total field F for magnetic storm, substorm, ULF, and polar-cap current studies

IMAGE EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Imager) wide-field ultraviolet imager measuring global plasmaspheric He+ column abundance and plasmapause structure via resonantly scattered 30.4 nm emission; three 30° sensor heads form an 84° × 30° fan swept by spacecraft spin to image cold-plasma morphology and dynamics with ~0.6° angular resolution and ~10 min cadence.

IMAGE RPI (Radio Plasma Imager) long-wire low-frequency radio sounder, relaxation sounder, and passive plasma-wave instrument measuring magnetospheric electron density structure, plasma resonances, direct/guided echo traces, and auroral kilometric radiation from 3 kHz to 3 MHz using active coded transmissions and long X/Y dipoles plus a Z-axis antenna

IMAGE HK (Housekeeping) spacecraft engineering and ancillary platform data product recording observatory status rather than heliophysics particles or fields, including attitude determination, Autonomous Star Tracker state, communications, flight software, power-system telemetry, and thermal housekeeping used to qualify IMAGE science observations

IMAGE (Imager for Magnetopause-to-Aurora Global Exploration) Ephemeris platform data product measuring spacecraft position and orbital location, the IMAGE Positions ancillary record giving geocentric location in multiple coordinate systems for timing, mapping, and contextualizing IMAGE remote-sensing and in situ observations in the magnetosphere

ISEE-3 Ephemeris (International Sun-Earth Explorer 3 spacecraft position) platform ephemeris data product reporting the spacecraft position vector in GSE (Geocentric Solar Ecliptic) coordinates for contextualizing ISEE-3 heliospheric, magnetospheric, and solar-wind measurements, not a particle or field sensor

ISEE-3 MAG (Magnetic Field Experiment) vector helium magnetometer measuring the steady interplanetary magnetic field and low-frequency variations; vector field ranges ±4, ±14, ±42, ±144, ±640, ±4000, ±22,000, and ±140,000 nT, with a single-axis spectrum analyzer for spin-axis fluctuations centered at 0.33, 3.2, and 8.8 Hz

ISEE-3 SWP (Solar Wind Plasma) electrostatic analyzer measuring unshocked solar-wind proton/ion and electron velocity distribution functions in 2-D and 3-D; ion/proton measurements covered roughly 0.15-7 keV, with channels spanning about 0.24-10.7 keV/q, and electrons covered ~10 eV-1 keV, including an 8.5-1140 eV range and commandable 1.6-220 eV photoelectron range

ISEE 1 MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic field components for magnetospheric, magnetosheath, and solar-wind studies, with selectable ±256 nT and ±8192 nT component ranges and science bandwidths from ~2 to 32 Hz depending on telemetry mode

ISEE 1 VES (Vector Electron Spectrometer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional electron velocity distribution functions with two triaxial sets of 127° cylindrical analyzers; nominal modes cover solar-wind electrons 7-500 eV, magnetosheath 10 eV-2 keV, and magnetotail/solar observations 105 eV-7.05 keV with ΔE/E ~0.07

ISEE 1 FPE (Fast Plasma Experiment) electrostatic analyzer plasma investigation measuring ion/proton and electron velocity distributions in the solar wind, bow shock, magnetosheath, magnetopause, magnetotail, and magnetosphere; flown with the SWE (Solar Wind Experiment) ion analyzer, covering protons/ions ~50 eV-40 keV and electrons ~5 eV-20 keV

ISEE 1 PWE (Plasma Wave Experiment) plasma-wave antenna/receiver investigation measuring electric and magnetic field fluctuations in the magnetosphere and solar wind; using 215 m, 73.5 m and 0.61 m electric dipoles plus a triaxial search coil, with sweep receiver 100 Hz-400 kHz, spectrum analyzer 5.62 Hz-311 kHz E and 5.62 Hz-10 kHz B, wave-normal analyzer 100 Hz-5 kHz, and wideband waveforms to 2 MHz

International Sun-Earth Explorer 2 (ISEE-2) MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic fields and magnetohydrodynamic waves in the solar wind, bow shock, magnetosheath, magnetopause and magnetosphere, with component ranges of ±256 nanotesla (nT) and ±8192 nT; companion to the matching ISEE-1 fluxgate magnetometer

ISEE-2 FPE (Fast Plasma Experiment) dual spherical electrostatic-analyzer plasma instrument measuring one-, two-, and three-dimensional ion and electron velocity distributions in the solar wind, bow shock, magnetosheath, magnetopause, and magnetotail; positive ions/protons 50 eV-40 keV and electrons 5 eV-20 keV, coordinated with the similar ISEE-1 FPE.

International Space Station AMS-02 (Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer-02) magnetic spectrometer measuring cosmic-ray charge, rigidity, momentum, velocity, energy and mass for electrons, positrons, protons, antiprotons, gamma rays and nuclei up to iron from ~0.5 GeV to multi-TeV; comprising TRD (Transition Radiation Detector), TOF (Time-of-Flight), Tracker, RICH (Ring Imaging Cherenkov), ECAL (Electromagnetic Calorimeter) and ACC (Anti-Coincidence Counters)

International Space Station TEPC (Tissue-Equivalent Proportional Counter) active radiation dosimeter, specifically a position-sensitive tissue-equivalent proportional chamber PS-TEPC, measuring absorbed dose, dose equivalent, dose rate, quality factor, and microdosimetric lineal-energy/LET spectra from trapped particles, galactic cosmic rays, solar energetic particles, and secondary neutrons inside ISS

International Space Station FPMU (Floating Potential Measurement Unit) Langmuir probe plasma diagnostic suite measuring station structure floating potential and local ionospheric electron density/temperature; comprising FPP (Floating Potential Probe), WLP (Wide Sweep Langmuir Probe), NLP (Narrow Sweep Langmuir Probe), and PIP (Plasma Impedance Probe) sensors on the station truss

Interball-1 MIF-M (Multicomponent Investigations of Fluctuations of Magnetic Fields) magnetometer measuring magnetic-field fluctuations on the Interball Tail Probe/ASPI fields-and-waves payload, using triaxial fluxgate channels for DC 0-2 Hz and AC 2-25 Hz fields plus a Z-axis search-coil channel from 1 Hz to 40 kHz and a seven-band analog filter bank.

Interball-1 FM-3I (Fluxgate direct-current magnetometer) dual fluxgate magnetometer measuring the spacecraft-frame vector magnetic field; comprising the M1 science sensor covering ±200 nT at 0.125-16 vectors/s and the M2 wide-range/attitude sensor covering ±1000 nT at 1 vector/6 s, with M2 failed after February 1996

Interball-1 FGMI (Fluxgate Magnetometer-I) ASPI fields-and-waves instrument measuring vector magnetic field and Langmuir split-probe plasma current on the Tail Probe; one of the ASPI sensors alongside MIF-M, OPERA, and PRAM, with magnetic range 0.3-37.5 nT, DC-2 Hz bandwidth, and 0.25-8 samples/s cadence.

Interball-1 AKR2 (Auroral Kilometric Radiation 2) shielded loop-antenna radio receiver measuring electromagnetic kilometric radio-emission intensity from 100 kHz to 1.5 MHz in six ~10 kHz channels centered at 100, 250, 500, 750, 1000, and 1500 kHz, rejecting local electrostatic perturbations to observe natural AKR and related emissions

Interball-1 CORALL (Wide-range 3D Ion Spectrometer) hemispherical electrostatic ion spectrometer measuring quasi-three-dimensional ion energy-per-charge distribution functions from 30 eV/q to 24.2 keV/q in 32 steps, using spacecraft spin with a 10°×150° fan field of view and five polar look directions at 45°, 70°, 95°, 120°, and 145° from the Sun.

Interball-1 ELECTRON (3D Electron Distribution Function) quadrispherical top-hat electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional plasma electron distribution functions from 10 eV to 26 keV, with 180° × 6° instantaneous field of view, 8 anode sectors, 22.5° × 6° angular sampling, and full 4π steradian coverage over a spacecraft spin in the magnetotail and magnetosphere

Interball-1 DOK-2 (Energetic Proton/Electron Spectrometer) energetic particle spectrometer measuring magnetospheric electrons at 20-420 keV and ions/protons at 20-850 keV; four silicon telescope channels in fixed antisolar and mechanically scanned look directions provide spin-resolved three-dimensional angular distributions and time profiles in the magnetotail and boundary regions

Interball-1 SKA-2 (Low and Energetic Charged Particle Composition and Anisotropy) energetic-particle ion spectrometer measuring solar wind H+ and He++ fluxes, composition, and energy-angular distributions near the Sun direction with high time resolution, supporting proton/alpha anisotropy studies in the magnetospheric tail environment

Interball-1 PROMICS-3 (Ion Composition 3D Spectrometer) toroidal electrostatic plasma mass spectrometer measuring three-dimensional ion distributions with mass separation M=1-32 from 4 eV to 70 keV and electron distributions from 12 eV to 35 keV; comprising the MEPS electron spectrometer and TRICS ion mass spectrometer on the Interball Tail Probe

Interball-1 VDP (Omnidirectional Plasma Sensor) Faraday cup array measuring magnetospheric ion or electron integral flux vectors and 16-step energy spectra from 0.2-2.4 keV; comprising six 134° full-angle cups looking Sunward +X, anti-Sun -X, and ±Y/±Z, with cup 1 ion-biased only and cups 4 and 6 generally unusable

Interball-1 Ephemeris spacecraft orbit data product providing the Interball-1/Tail Probe position and velocity versus time for locating in situ plasma, magnetic-field, energetic-particle, and wave measurements in geocentric coordinates, especially high-apogee magnetotail, magnetopause, and solar-wind context intervals

Magion-4 Ephemeris (spacecraft orbit) platform/ancillary data product providing time-tagged Magion-4 spacecraft position, velocity, and orbital context for the Czech subsatellite of the Interball tail mission, used to place plasma, field, and wave observations in geocentric/magnetospheric coordinates; not a science detector or sensor

Juno Ephemeris (Juno Positions) platform trajectory product providing time-tagged Juno spacecraft position and velocity rather than particle or field measurements, used to locate Juno in interplanetary space and the Jovian system for solar-wind, bow-shock, magnetopause, magnetosphere, and conjunction context studies

LANL Spacecraft Series (1990–2004) MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer, flown on LANL-1990/Los Alamos National Laboratory 1990-095 geosynchronous spacecraft, measuring spin-resolved three-dimensional ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions from ~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q and deriving plasma spectra and moments for magnetospheric plasma studies

LANL Spacecraft Series (1990–2004) SOPA (Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer) energetic particle spectrometer at geosynchronous orbit, including LANL-1990/LANL 1990-095, measuring trapped and injected magnetospheric electrons (50 keV–1.5 MeV, integral >1.5 MeV), protons (50 keV–50 MeV), alpha particles, and CNO/heavy ions as directional differential fluxes with three silicon-telescope look directions per spin

LANL Spacecraft Series LANL 1991 (1991–2008) MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional geosynchronous plasma ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions from ~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q, individual Los Alamos National Laboratory spacecraft-series unit cited as LANL-1991 or 1991-080 MPA

LANL Spacecraft Series LANL-1991 (1991–2008) SOPA (Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer), silicon solid-state energetic-particle telescope on Los Alamos National Laboratory geosynchronous spacecraft launched in 1991, measuring spin-resolved directional electron/ion fluxes at 3 look angles: protons 50 keV–50 MeV; electrons 50 keV–1.5 MeV + >1.5 MeV integral; alpha 0.5–1.3, carbon-nitrogen-oxygen 1.5–3.55, carbon 5–13, nitrogen 6–14, oxygen 7.2–15 MeV; sulfur >8 MeV; bromine >15 MeV

LANL Spacecraft Series 1994 (1994–2007), LANL 1994-084 MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions at geosynchronous orbit from ~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q, used for plasma moments, spacecraft-potential studies, and pitch-angle/azimuthal distributions in the inner magnetosphere

LANL Spacecraft Series (1994–2007) SOPA (Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer) energetic particle telescope, including LANL-1994 (1994-084), on LANL geosynchronous spacecraft measuring spin-resolved electron and ion fluxes in three look directions: e− 50 keV–1.5 MeV plus >1.5 MeV integral, p 50 keV–50 MeV, α 0.5–1.3 MeV, CNO 1.5–3.55 MeV, C 5–13 MeV, N 6–14 MeV, O 7.2–15 MeV, S >8 MeV, Br >15 MeV

LANL Spacecraft Series LANL 1997 (1997–2008) MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer), electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions at geosynchronous orbit from ~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q, sampling hot magnetospheric plasma, plasma sheet, ring-current, and spacecraft-environment populations

LANL Spacecraft Series SOPA (Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer), including LANL-1997 (1997–2008), energetic particle telescope on LANL geosynchronous/synchronous-orbit spacecraft measuring energetic GEO electron, proton, and ion fluxes in three look directions; differential electrons 50 keV–1.5 MeV plus >1.5 MeV integral, protons 50 keV–50 MeV, alpha 0.5–1.3 MeV, CNO 1.5–3.55 MeV, C/N/O to ~15 MeV, integral S >8 MeV and Br >15 MeV

LANL Spacecraft Series (1989–2007) LANL 1989/1989-046 MPA (Magnetospheric Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer on the 1989 LANL geosynchronous spacecraft-series unit, measuring spin-resolved three-dimensional ion and electron energy-per-charge distributions, angular/pitch-angle distributions, and plasma moments at geosynchronous orbit over ~1 eV/q to >40 keV/q.

LANL Spacecraft Series (1989–2007) SOPA (Synchronous Orbit Particle Analyzer) energetic-particle telescope, flown on LANL geosynchronous spacecraft including LANL 1989-046/LANL-1989, measuring spin-resolved electron and ion fluxes with three telescopes: e− 50 keV–1.5 MeV differential and >1.5 MeV integral; p 50 keV–50 MeV; α 0.5–1.3 MeV; CNO 1.5–3.55 MeV; C 5–13, N 6–14, O 7.2–15, S >8, Br >15 MeV integral

MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution) spacecraft ephemeris ancillary data product providing the orbiter trajectory and observing geometry at Mars, including spacecraft position and velocity, altitude, latitude/longitude, local solar time, solar zenith angle, and Mars-centered coordinate context used to colocate MAVEN science measurements

MESSENGER (MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry, and Ranging) ephemeris platform product measuring/reporting spacecraft position and velocity versus time, used to locate spacecraft and in-situ observations along Mercury cruise and orbital trajectories in Mercury-centered, Mercury solar orbital, Mercury solar electric, or heliocentric coordinates

MESSENGER (Mercury Surface, Space Environment, Geochemistry, and Ranging) MAG (Magnetometer) three-axis fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic fields at Mercury and in the solar wind, with selectable cadences from 0.01 to 40 Hz for DC fields and magnetic-field fluctuations in Mercury’s magnetosphere, magnetosheath, cusps, tail, and upstream IMF.

MetOp-B (2012–present) SEM-2 (Space Environmental Monitor-2) energetic-particle spectrometer measuring charged-particle fluxes, radiation-belt intensity, and auroral/radiation-belt electrons/ions in low Earth orbit at satellite altitude; TED (Total Energy Detector) 0.05–20 keV electron/proton bands and MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector) 0°/90° telescopes: e− >30/>100/>300 keV, p P1–P5 30–6900 keV, plus omnidirectional high-energy proton response

MetOp-A (2006–2021) SEM-2 (Space Environmental Monitor-2) multi-channel energetic charged-particle spectrometer measuring satellite-altitude/low-Earth-orbit auroral and radiation-belt particle fluxes and radiation-belt intensity; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector, electrons and ions in 0.05–20 keV bands), MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector, electrons/protons/ions from ~30 keV to >6.9 MeV), and a common processing unit.

MMS-1 ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument regulating positive spacecraft charging by emitting indium ion beams, typically holding potential below about +4 V to improve low-energy plasma and electric-field measurements by FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation), HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer), ADP (axial double probe), and SDP (spin-plane double probe)

MMS-1 DSP (Digital Signal Processor) FIELDS wave-processing instrument measuring electric- and magnetic-field fluctuations by digitizing SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) signals for waveform, spectral, burst, and Solitary Wave Detector products; one FIELDS suite element alongside FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

MMS-1 (Magnetospheric Multiscale) SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) AC magnetometer measuring three-axis magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from ~1 Hz to 6 kHz; one of the FIELDS suite sensors alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe)

MMS-1 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 1) ADP (Axial Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring the spin-axis electric-field component for 3-D DC to 100 kHz electric fields; part of the FIELDS suite alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), DFG (digital fluxgate magnetometer), AFG (analog fluxgate magnetometer), SCM (search-coil magnetometer), and EDI (electron drift instrument)

MMS-1 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 1) SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring the two spin-plane components of DC-to-100 kHz electric fields and spacecraft-potential/plasma-density variations; one FIELDS-suite electric double probe alongside ADP (Axial Double Probe), with sibling AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

MMS-1 EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), one sensor of the Magnetospheric Multiscale FIELDS suite alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), DFG/AFG (digital/analog fluxgate magnetometers) and SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), uses coded ~1 keV electron beams from two GDUs (Gun Detector Units) to measure electron drift, convection electric field, and magnetic field magnitude/direction

MMS-1 EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer) energetic particle spectrometer measuring energetic ion flux, spectra, composition, and angular/pitch-angle distributions, one of the Magnetospheric Multiscale Energetic Particle Detector suite instruments alongside FEEPS (Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Spectrometer); resolves mainly H+ and O+ ions over ~45-500 keV at ~30 s composition cadence

MMS-1 FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer in the FIELDS suite measuring DC vector magnetic fields and current structures at electron and ion diffusion scales; comprising redundant AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer) and DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer) sensors, alongside FIELDS siblings SCM, EDP, and EDI on Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 1

MMS-1 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 1) FEEPS (Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Sensor) energetic particle telescope in the EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) suite alongside EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer), using two fly’s-eye sensor heads to measure 3-D energetic electron (~25–500 keV) and ion (~45–500 keV) flux distributions at ~10 s cadence

MMS-1 DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer set in the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite, one of the plasma sensors alongside DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers), measuring 3-D electron velocity distribution functions, energy spectra, pitch-angle distributions, and density/temperature/flow moments from ~10 eV to 30 keV at 30 ms cadence

MMS-1 DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers) electrostatic analyser set measuring three-dimensional ion velocity distributions, densities, velocities, and temperatures from ~10 eV/q to 30 keV/q at 150 ms cadence; the ion sensor complement of the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite on MMS-1 alongside the DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers) electron sensors

MMS-1 HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer) electrostatic/time-of-flight ion mass spectrometer measuring three-dimensional magnetospheric ion composition, fluxes, and velocity distributions for H+, He+, He++, and O+ from ~1 eV/q to 40 keV/q, with radio-frequency mass filtering for minor ions during reconnection intervals

MMS-1 Ephemeris (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 1 ephemeris) platform/ancillary data product providing spacecraft position, velocity, orbit state, and location in geocentric coordinate systems for MMS-1, often used with MEC mission ephemeris and coordinates data to contextualize MMS plasma, fields, boundary-crossing, and constellation-separation observations

MMS-2 ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument measuring and regulating spacecraft charging by emitting indium ion beams to hold the observatory near ≤+4 V, enabling accurate low-energy plasma and electric-field measurements by FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation), HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe); two ASPOC units fly on MMS-2

MMS-2 FIELDS/DSP (Digital Signal Processor) waveform/spectral processor measuring AC electric-field and search-coil magnetic-field waves (~1 Hz-6 kHz), a MMS-2 FIELDS suite component with SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer) and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument); produces waveforms, spectra, spectral matrices and SWD (Solitary Wave Detector) triggers

MMS-2 SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring three-axis AC magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from ~1 Hz to 6 kHz; one of the MMS-2 FIELDS suite sensors alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), and ADP (Axial Double Probe)

MMS-2 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 2) ADP (Axial Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field sensor measuring the spin-axis electric field and spacecraft potential fluctuations from DC to 100 kHz; one of the FIELDS electric double probes alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), with AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

MMS-2 SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring DC and wave electric fields in the spacecraft spin plane from quasi-static to 100 kHz; part of the FIELDS suite with ADP (Axial Double Probe), AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

MMS-2 EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-beam drift instrument measuring DC convection electric field, E×B drift, and magnetic-field geometry using coded ~1 keV electron beams; one of the MMS-2 FIELDS suite sensors alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), and ADP (Axial Double Probe)

MMS-2 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 2) EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer) energetic particle instrument measuring energetic ion spectra, angular distributions, and composition, especially H+ protons and O+ oxygen ions, over ~45-500 keV with ~30 s cadence; one of the MMS-2 EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) suite sensors alongside FEEPS (Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Sensor)

MMS-2 FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) dual fluxgate magnetometer measuring high-cadence DC vector magnetic fields for magnetopause and magnetotail reconnection/current structure; part of the Magnetospheric Multiscale FIELDS suite alongside EDP (Electric Double Probe), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), comprising redundant AFG (Analog Fluxgate) and DFG (Digital Fluxgate) sensors

MMS-2 FEEPS (Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Spectrometer) energetic particle telescope array measuring 3-D energetic electron and ion flux, spectra, and pitch-angle distributions, ~25-650 keV electrons and ~45-650 keV ions; one of the MMS Energetic Particle Detector suite sensors alongside EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer)

MMS-2 DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer, the electron sensor complement of the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite alongside DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers), comprising four dual-head electron spectrometers measuring 3D electron velocity distributions and moments from ~10 eV to 30 keV with 30 ms cadence for magnetic-reconnection plasma studies

MMS-2 DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer ion sensor set of the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite, alongside the DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers), measuring three-dimensional ion velocity distribution functions, moments, density, bulk velocity and temperature from ~10 eV to 30 keV at up to 150 ms cadence.

MMS-2 HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer) ion composition spectrometer measuring three-dimensional hot-plasma ion fluxes and velocity distributions of H+, He+, He2+, and O+ from ~1 eV/q to 40 keV/q, using electrostatic energy analysis and time-of-flight mass-per-charge discrimination for magnetopause and magnetotail reconnection studies

MMS-2 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 2) Ephemeris ancillary platform data product giving the spacecraft orbit state, position, velocity, and timing used to locate MMS-2 in geocentric solar ecliptic (GSE), geocentric solar magnetospheric (GSM), or inertial coordinates for conjunctions and interpretation of MMS particle, fields, and plasma measurements

MMS-3 DSP (Digital Signal Processor) FIELDS suite wave processor measuring electric- and magnetic-field waveforms and spectra from the SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), including onboard filtering, spectral products, burst wave capture, and Solitary Wave Detector event selection alongside AFG, DFG, EDI, and CIDP.

MMS-3 SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring three-axis AC magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from ~1 Hz to 6 kHz; one FIELDS suite sensor on Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 3 alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), EDP (Electric Double Probe: SDP and ADP), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

MMS-3 ADP (Axial Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring the spacecraft spin-axis electric-field component from DC to ~100 kHz; one of the MMS-3 FIELDS suite sensors alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), AFG/DFG fluxgate magnetometers, and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer)

MMS-3 SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe) double-probe electric-field instrument measuring spin-plane DC and wave electric fields to ~100 kHz with four spherical sensors on 48 m wire booms; the spin-plane EDP (Electric Double Probe) sensor in the MMS-3 FIELDS suite with ADP (Axial Double Probe), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), AFG (Analog Fluxgate Magnetometer), DFG (Digital Fluxgate Magnetometer), and SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer)

MMS-3 (Magnetospheric Multiscale) EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron-beam drift instrument in the FIELDS suite measuring DC electric field, E×B convection velocity, and magnetic field from ~1 keV test-electron gyromotion/time of flight; sibling FIELDS sensors are AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), and EDP (Electric Double Probe: SDP spin-plane, ADP axial).

MMS-3 EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer) energetic particle telescope measuring energetic ion spectra, angular/pitch-angle distributions, and composition (especially H+ and O+) at ~45-500 keV with ~30 s cadence; one of the MMS Energetic Particle Detector suite sensors alongside FEEPS (Fly’s Eye Energetic Particle Sensor)

MMS-3 (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 3) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) vector magnetometer measuring quasi-static magnetic field strength and direction; a FIELDS suite sensor alongside SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), EDP (Electric Double Probe: SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe) and ADP (Axial Double Probe)), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), combining AFG (Analog Fluxgate) and DFG (Digital Fluxgate) sensors

MMS-3 FEEPS (Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Spectrometer) energetic particle instrument measuring three-dimensional energetic electron and ion flux distributions, one of the MMS Energetic Particle Detector suite sensors alongside EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer); two FEEPS heads cover electrons ~25-500 keV and ions ~45-500 keV at ~10 s cadence on MMS-3.

MMS-3 DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer set measuring 3-D electron velocity distributions, moments, and pitch-angle distributions from ~10 eV to 30 keV at up to 30 ms cadence; the electron sensor complement of the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite on MMS-3, comprising four DES heads alongside four DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers) ion sensors and the IDPU (Instrument Data Processing Unit)

MMS-3 DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer group measuring three-dimensional ion velocity distributions, density, bulk velocity, and temperature from ~10 eV to 30 keV at up to 150 ms cadence; the ion sensor set of the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite on Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 3, alongside the DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers) electron analyzers

MMS-3 HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer) particle detector measuring three-dimensional hot ion composition and velocity distributions for H+, He++, He+, and O+ from ~1 eV/q to 40 keV/q, with electrostatic energy analysis and time-of-flight mass discrimination for magnetospheric and magnetopause reconnection plasmas

MMS-3 Ephemeris (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 3 ephemeris) platform/orbit data product, not a particle or field sensor, providing spacecraft position and velocity versus time for the third MMS observatory, commonly in GSE/GSM/geocentric coordinates, for locating MMS-3 measurements and formation separations.

MMS-4 ASPOC (Active Spacecraft Potential Control) spacecraft-potential control instrument stabilizing spacecraft potential, using two indium ion emitter units to limit positive charging to about +4 V and improve low-energy plasma/electric-field measurements by FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation), HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer), ADP (axial double probe), and SDP (spin-plane double probe)

MMS-4 DSP (Digital Signal Processor) FIELDS suite onboard signal-processing unit measuring electric-field and AC magnetic-field waveforms/spectra by digitizing and processing SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) signals, including spectral products and SWD (Solitary Wave Detector) event capture.

MMS-4 SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring three-axis AC magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from ~1 Hz to 6 kHz; one of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite sensors alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), ADP (Axial Double Probe), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument)

MMS-4 ADP (Axial Double Probe) double-sphere electric-field instrument measuring the spin-axis electric-field component from DC to 100 kHz; part of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite alongside SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), AFG/DFG (Analog/Digital Fluxgate Magnetometers), and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), enabling full 3-D electric fields when combined with SDP.

MMS-4 SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe) double-probe electric-field instrument measuring two spin-plane components of DC–100 kHz electric fields with ~0.5 mV/m accuracy; part of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite alongside ADP (Axial Double Probe), EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), AFG/DFG fluxgate magnetometers, and SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer)

MMS-4 EDI (Electron Drift Instrument) electron drift instrument measuring convection electric field and magnetic-field magnitude from the drift/return of coded ~1 keV electron beams; part of the MMS-4 FIELDS suite alongside AFG (Analog Fluxgate), DFG (Digital Fluxgate), SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer), SDP (Spin-plane Double Probe), and ADP (Axial Double Probe).

MMS-4 EIS (Energetic Ion Spectrometer) energetic particle instrument measuring energetic ion fluxes, angular distributions, and H/He/O composition at ~45-500 keV with 30 s cadence; one of the MMS EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) suite sensors alongside FEEPS (Fly’s Eye Energetic Particle Sensor), with PHxTOF and ExTOF ion products.

MMS-4 FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) magnetometer measuring DC magnetic-field vectors for reconnection and current structures; part of the FIELDS suite alongside EDP (Electric Double Probe), SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), and EDI (Electron Drift Instrument), with redundant AFG (Analog Fluxgate) and DFG (Digital Fluxgate) sensors, typically used at 128 vectors/s burst cadence

MMS-4 FEEPS (Fly's Eye Energetic Particle Spectrometer) energetic-particle sensor, one of the MMS-4 EPD (Energetic Particle Detector) suite instruments alongside EIS, measuring near-3D energetic electron and ion flux/pitch-angle distributions at ~25-500 keV for electrons and ~45-500 keV for ions

MMS-4 DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers) electrostatic analyzer array, the electron sensor set of the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite alongside DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers), measuring 3-D electron velocity distributions, moments, and pitch-angle/energy spectra from ~10 eV to 30 keV at up to 30 ms cadence in burst mode.

MMS-4 DIS (Dual Ion Spectrometers), electrostatic analyzer ion sensor set in the FPI (Fast Plasma Investigation) suite alongside the DES (Dual Electron Spectrometers), measuring three-dimensional ion velocity distribution functions and moments—density, bulk flow, and temperature—from ~10 eV to 30 keV at 150 ms cadence.

MMS-4 HPCA (Hot Plasma Composition Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer/time-of-flight ion composition spectrometer measuring 3-D ion velocity distributions, fluxes, and moments for H+, He++, He+, and O+ from ~1 eV/q to 40 keV/q, resolving solar-wind and magnetospheric plasma populations during reconnection studies

MMS-4 Ephemeris (Magnetospheric Multiscale spacecraft 4 ephemeris) platform ancillary data product providing MMS-4 spacecraft position, velocity, orbit state, and coordinate-transformed location (commonly GSE, GSM, SM/GEO) used to place fields and particles measurements and determine constellation separations in magnetospheric studies

Mars Science Laboratory MSL (Mars Science Laboratory) Ephemeris virtual platform product providing spacecraft, cruise-stage, and Curiosity rover position/trajectory coordinates versus time for geometry, conjunction, and context analyses, rather than an in situ or remote-sensing science instrument measuring plasma or fields.

Munin MEDUSA (Miniaturized Electrostatic DUal-tophat Spherical Analyser) electrostatic analyzer measuring simultaneous auroral electrons and ions up to 17 keV/q, returning energy spectra and 16-sector angular distributions in the acceptance plane aligned with Earth’s magnetic field, with electron sweeps at 4 s^-1 and ion sweeps at 2 s^-1

Munin Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris platform data product measuring the Munin spacecraft orbital state—time-tagged position, velocity, altitude, latitude/longitude, and geomagnetic or magnetospheric location—used to contextualize Munin particle and auroral observations rather than a separate fields or particle sensor

Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution (MAVEN) LPW (Langmuir Probe and Waves) Langmuir probe, electric-field/waves, and solar EUV photometer investigation measuring ionospheric electron density and temperature, spacecraft-potential/plasma waves and fields (0.05-10 Hz, 90 kHz-1.6 MHz; ±50 V sweeps), and solar irradiance in 0.1-7 nm, 17-22 nm, and H Lyman-alpha 121.6 nm channels

MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution) EUV (Extreme Ultraviolet Monitor) broadband photometer/radiometer measuring solar soft X-ray and ultraviolet irradiance at Mars; part of the LPW (Langmuir Probe and Waves) investigation alongside the dual Langmuir probes, with Channel A 0.1-3 nm and 17-22 nm, Channel B 0.1-7 nm, and Channel C Lyman-alpha 121-122 nm at 1 s cadence

Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution (MAVEN) MAG (Magnetometer) dual fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic-field magnitude and direction in the solar wind, Martian induced magnetosphere/ionosphere, and crustal anomaly regions; two solar-panel-tip sensors provide ranges ±512 nT (0.015625 nT), ±2048 nT (0.0625 nT), and ±65536 nT (2 nT)

Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution NGIMS (Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectrometer) quadrupole mass spectrometer measuring in situ thermal neutral and positive ion composition and isotopes in the Martian upper atmosphere (~120-500 km), using closed and open ion sources over 2-150 amu for He, N, CO, N2, NO, O2, Ar, CO2 and ions O2+, CO2+, NO+, O+, CO+, C+, N2+, OH+, N+

MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution) SEP (Solar Energetic Particle) solid-state telescope instrument measuring energetic electron and proton fluxes, spectra, and angular distributions at Mars; comprising SEP1 and SEP2 orthogonal dual-ended silicon telescopes providing four look directions, with proton channels 25 keV-6 MeV, electron channels 25 keV-1 MeV, flux dynamic range ~20-10^7 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1, and 2-32 s cadences

Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution (MAVEN) STATIC (SupraThermal And Thermal Ion Composition) electrostatic analyzer with time-of-flight mass analysis measuring Martian ion composition and 3-D energy–pitch-angle distributions from cold ionospheric ions to pickup ions, ~0.1 eV/q to 30 keV/q, mass 1-70 amu, including H+, He++, O+, O2+, and CO2+ escape populations

Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution (MAVEN) SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional solar wind, magnetosheath, and Martian ionospheric electron energy-angle and pitch-angle distributions over ~3 eV-4.6 keV (often cited as 5 eV-5 keV) with a wide ~360° × 120° field of view

MAVEN (Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN) SWIA (Solar Wind Ion Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring in situ solar-wind and planetary ion energy flux, angular distributions, density, bulk velocity, and temperature around Mars over ~5 eV/q–25 keV/q, 30–2000 km/s flow speeds, with 360° × 90° field of view and ~4 s survey cadence

New Horizons SWAP (Solar Wind Around Pluto) plasma ion spectrometer measuring solar wind ions and Pluto pickup/escape ions from ~25 eV/q to 7.5 keV/q; combines a cylindrically symmetric retarding potential analyzer (RPA) with a top-hat electrostatic analyzer and deflectors for wide-angle ion energy-per-charge spectra during spacecraft scans

NOAA 5 SPM (Solar Proton Monitor) energetic-particle telescope measuring solar energetic particle fluxes: directional protons in five contiguous channels from 0.15-40 MeV (thresholds 0.15, 0.30, 0.60, 1.5, 6.6 MeV) plus 400-600, 600-1000 and >1000 MeV; alphas 0.6-100 MeV (thresholds 0.60, 0.90, 1.4, 3.5, 11 MeV), 330-600 and >600 MeV; electrons >250 keV; omnidirectional protons >10, >30 and >60 MeV

NOAA 6 SEM (Space Environment Monitor) energetic particle suite measuring upper-atmosphere electrons, protons, and alpha particles; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector, e−/p 300 eV–20 keV), MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector, p 30 keV–>2.5 MeV, e− >30/>100/>300 keV, p/e >6 MeV, omni p >16/>36/>80 MeV), and HEPAT (High Energy Proton and Alpha Telescope, p >370 MeV, alpha >850 MeV/nucleon)

NOAA-7 SEM (Space Environment Monitor) energetic particle suite measuring upper-atmosphere, radiation-belt and solar-particle electron, proton and alpha fluxes; comprising TED (total energy detector, 300 eV-20 keV electrons/protons), MEPED (medium-energy proton and electron detector: protons 30 keV->2.5 MeV, electrons >30/>100/>300 keV, mixed >6 MeV, omni protons >16/>36/>80 MeV) and HEPAT/HEPAD high-energy proton-alpha telescope/detector (>370 MeV protons, >850 MeV/nucleon alphas)

NOAA-8 SEM (Space Environment Monitor) energetic particle suite measuring auroral and radiation-belt electrons, protons, and alpha particles; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector, 300 eV-20 keV electrons/protons), MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector, electrons >30/>100/>300 keV, protons 30 keV to >80 MeV), and HEPAD (High Energy Proton and Alpha Detector, protons >370 MeV, alphas >850 MeV/nucleon)

NOAA-10 (1986–1991) SEM (Space Environmental Monitor) particle detector in low Earth orbit measuring energetic precipitating/trapped electron and proton fluxes and spectra; includes MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector) protons 30 keV–>2.5 MeV, electrons >30/>100/>300 keV, mixed >6 MeV and omni protons >16/>36/>80 MeV, plus TED (Total Energy Detector) 300 eV–20 keV electrons/protons

NOAA-12 (1991–2007) SEM (Space Environment Monitor) energetic particle instrument suite measuring energetic proton and electron fluxes and energy spectra, including auroral and radiation-belt electrons and protons in low Earth orbit; comprising MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector), protons 30 keV to >2.5 MeV plus >16, >36, >80 MeV omnidirectional channels and electrons >30, >100, >300 keV, and TED (Total Energy Detector), electrons/protons 300 eV–20 keV

NOAA 14 (1994–2005) SEM (Space Environmental Monitor) energetic particle suite/monitor on the NOAA-J polar-orbiting spacecraft measuring near-Earth auroral/radiation-belt proton and electron fluxes and energy spectra; TED (Total Energy Detector): 300 eV–20 keV electrons/ions; MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector): protons 30 keV–>60 MeV, electrons >30/>100/>300 keV, >6 MeV integral particles, omnidirectional protons >16/>36/>80 MeV

NOAA 15 (1998–2020) SEM-2 (Space Environment Monitor-2) energetic particle suite measuring radiation-belt populations and trapped/precipitating auroral charged particles—electrons, protons, and ions; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector; electron/proton electrostatic analyzers, 50 eV-20 keV) and MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector; directional electrons >30, >100, >300 keV, protons ~30 keV-6.9 MeV, plus omnidirectional high-energy proton channels)

NOAA 16 (2000–2014) SEM-2 (Space Environment Monitor-2) energetic particle suite on the NOAA KLM polar orbiter, measuring near-Earth radiation-belt populations, auroral precipitation, and precipitating charged particles; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector) electron/ion electrostatic analyzers (~50 eV–20 keV) and MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector) telescopes for electrons >30, >100, >300 keV and protons/ions ~30 keV to >6.9 MeV plus omnidirectional MeV protons

NOAA 18 (2005–present) SEM-2 (Space Environment Monitor-2) energetic particle instrument measuring radiation-belt populations and auroral precipitating charged particles in polar orbit; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector) for electrons and ions/protons 50 eV–20 keV and MEPED (Medium Energy Proton/Electron Detector) for electrons >30, >100, >300 keV and protons/ions ~30 keV–>6.9 MeV, with higher-energy omnidirectional proton channels

NOAA 19 (2009–present) SEM-2 (Space Environment Monitor-2) energetic particle instrument measuring radiation-belt particles and auroral charged-particle precipitation—electrons, protons, and ions—on the NOAA-N Prime polar orbiter launched 2009; comprising TED (Total Energy Detector, 50 eV–20 keV swept analyzers) and MEPED (Medium Energy Proton and Electron Detector, 0°/90° telescopes for electrons >30, >100, >300 keV and protons 30 keV–6.9 MeV, plus omnidirectional protons to >140 MeV)

OMNI OMNI virtual instrument proxy for the multi-spacecraft near-Earth solar wind data set, measuring interplanetary magnetic field, solar wind plasma moments, and energetic particle fluxes using selected source magnetometers, electrostatic analyzers, and particle detectors from ACE, Wind, IMP-8, Geotail, GOES, and other missions

Wind Ephemeris (spacecraft position) platform data product measuring the Wind observatory location and orbit context, providing time-tagged position vectors in common geocentric and heliocentric frames such as Geocentric Solar Ecliptic (GSE), Geocentric Solar Magnetospheric (GSM), Geocentric Equatorial Inertial (GEI), and heliocentric ecliptic/inertial coordinates rather than a particle or field sensor

Wind MFI (Magnetic Field Investigation) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector interplanetary and near-Earth magnetic fields, with range settings from ±4 nT to ±65,536 nT per axis and products including 0.0226 s snapshot, 0.092 s detail, 3 s, 1 min and 1 h averages, 10.9 vectors/s standard data, 44 vectors/s snapshot data, and FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) spectra

Wind SWE (Solar Wind Experiment) Faraday-cup and electrostatic-analyzer suite measuring solar wind proton/ion moments and electron velocity distributions; comprising two ion Faraday cups (5 eV-5 keV), VEIS (Vector Electron Ion Spectrometer; ions 30 eV-30 keV, electrons 7 eV-30 keV), and the SES (Strahl Electron Spectrometer) for field-aligned/strahl electrons.

Phobos 2 Ephemeris spacecraft position data product providing Phobos 2 trajectory, spacecraft location, and timing context for Mars/Phobos mission observations, used to relate plasma, magnetic-field, wave, and particle measurements to spacecraft position in interplanetary space and near Mars/Phobos

Pioneer 10/11 MAG (Magnetic Fields) triaxial helium vector magnetometer measuring DC vector magnetic fields in the solar wind and planetary magnetospheres, with seven dynamic ranges from ±2.5 nT to ±10 gauss and data commonly reported in RTN coordinates; used for interplanetary, Jovian, and Pioneer 11 Saturn magnetic-field studies

Pioneer 10/11 PLS (Plasma Science) quadrispherical electrostatic analyzer measuring solar wind ion and electron distribution parameters, bulk speed, density, and temperature; dual 90° analyzers covered protons/ions from 0.1–18 keV and electrons from ~1–500 eV, with a high-resolution ion analyzer and a medium-energy ion/electron analyzer.

Pioneer 10 Ephemeris (spacecraft ephemeris) platform data product measuring/time-tagging Pioneer 10 spacecraft position and trajectory, typically as heliocentric or Earth-referenced coordinates and distance, for the 1972 Jupiter-flyby and outer-heliosphere Pioneer unit; contextual ephemeris, not a fields or particles science sensor.

Pioneer 11 MAG1 (Magnetic Fields) triaxial helium vector magnetometer measuring interplanetary and planetary magnetic-field strength and direction during the Jupiter/Saturn cruise and encounters, with seven autoranges spanning ±2.5 nT to ±1.0×10^-3 T and vector data commonly reported in RTN heliocentric coordinates

Pioneer 11 PLS (Plasma Science) quadrispherical plasma analyzer measuring solar-wind and planetary plasma ion/electron distributions, density, speed, temperature, and flux; dual 90° quadrispherical electrostatic analyzers: a 26-channeltron high-resolution ion analyzer for protons ~0.1-18 keV and a 5-collector medium-energy analyzer for ions and electrons, with electrons ~1-500 eV

Pioneer 11 Ephemeris (spacecraft positions) platform ephemeris data product measuring spacecraft location, trajectory, and observing geometry versus time, used to contextualize Pioneer 11 field, plasma, and particle measurements during interplanetary cruise and the Jupiter, Saturn, and outer-heliosphere encounters

Pioneer Venus Orbiter OMAG (Orbiter Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic fields at Venus and in the solar wind, resolving planetary/remanent fields, ionospheric currents, the induced magnetosphere, bow shock and near wake; returned 3-axis vectors at up to 4 Hz near periapsis and 8-32 s cadence elsewhere

Pioneer Venus Orbiter ORPA (Orbiter Retarding Potential Analyzer) Langmuir-probe retarding potential analyzer measuring Venus ionospheric electron density and temperature, major ion concentrations and temperatures, ion drift velocities, and ambient photoelectron energy distributions with multigrid cup sensors operated in electron, ion, or photoelectron modes

Pioneer Venus Orbiter PVO (Pioneer Venus Orbiter) ephemeris/platform position data product providing spacecraft trajectory, position, and timing context rather than sensor measurements, used to locate PVO plasma, field, and particle observations in Venus-centered and heliocentric space for comparison with Venus solar wind and magnetosheath regions

Pioneer Venus Orbiter OPA (Orbiter Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring solar-wind, magnetosheath, ionopause, and wake ion and electron distributions; quadrispherical analyzer covering ions 50 eV/q–8 keV/q in 32 steps and electrons 1–500 eV in 16 steps over ±85° elevation and 360° azimuth.

Polar HYDRA (Hot Plasma Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer measuring three-dimensional electron and ion distribution functions, fluxes, moments, and pitch-angle structure in magnetospheric and auroral plasmas from ~1 eV to 30 keV with 0.5 s resolution, using body-mounted and loss-cone analyzer heads for cusp, entry-layer, reconnection, and field-aligned-current studies.
