POLAR EFI (Electric Fields Investigation) double-probe electric-field instrument measuring three-component quasi-static and low-frequency electric fields, spacecraft potential, convection fields, auroral parallel/perpendicular fields, double layers, and electrostatic shocks; uses three orthogonal double probes: 160 m spin-plane spherical, 350 m effective spin-plane cylindrical, and 14 m axial spherical pairs.

POLAR Ephemeris (orbit) platform data product providing the Polar spacecraft position, velocity, and time-tagged geocentric trajectory for contextualizing high-inclination, highly elliptical magnetospheric observations, including location relative to Earth, bow shock, magnetopause, auroral acceleration, cusp, and polar magnetosphere regions

Polar CAMMICE (Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment) energetic-particle ion composition suite measuring magnetospheric ion mass, charge, energy spectra, and angular distributions from <10 keV/Q to 15 MeV/Q for H through Fe; comprising MICS (Magnetospheric Ion Composition Sensor) and HIT (Heavy Ion Telescope), used for plasma-sheet and ring-current populations

Polar PWI (Plasma Wave Investigation) waveform receiver measuring naturally occurring and active-experiment electromagnetic and electrostatic plasma waves along the Polar orbit, with magnetic fields from 1 Hz-400 kHz, electric fields from 1 Hz-3.2 MHz, and density fluctuations from 1 Hz-16 kHz, including six-component waveform captures for wave normal, polarization, and Poynting-vector analysis

Polar TIDE (Thermal Ion Dynamics Experiment) low-energy ion mass spectrometer measuring cold magnetospheric and ionospheric ion velocity distributions, flows, and composition, including H+, He+, O+ and heavier ions, over ~0-100 eV/q and mass/charge ~1-64 amu/q with full distributions each 6-s spin; often used with the Polar PSI (Plasma Source Instrument) potential-control system

Polar TIMAS (Toroidal Imaging Mass-Angle Spectrograph) ion mass-angle spectrograph measuring full 3D velocity distributions of major magnetospheric ions, including H+, He++, He+ and O+, over mass/charge 1 to >32 amu/e and energy/charge ~15 eV/e to 32 keV/e, with near-4π angular coverage each half spin for cusp, auroral, ring-current and plasma-sheet studies.

Polar CAMMICE-MICS (Charge and Mass Magnetospheric Ion Composition Experiment Magnetospheric Ion Composition Sensor) energetic particle mass spectrometer measuring magnetospheric ion charge state, mass, and incident energy from ~1 keV/e to 420 keV/e; one of the CAMMICE suite sensors alongside HIT (Heavy Ion Telescope), using energy-per-charge, time-of-flight, and residual energy to identify ion composition

Polar CEPPAD (Comprehensive Energetic Particle Pitch Angle Distribution) energetic-particle investigation measuring full pitch-angle distributions of electrons (20 keV-3 MeV), protons (20 keV-17 MeV), and helium/CNO ions (30-3300 keV/nucleon); comprising the IPS (Imaging Proton Sensor), IES (Imaging Electron Sensor), and HIST (High-Sensitivity Telescope)

POLAR MFE (Magnetic Fields Experiment) fluxgate magnetometer measuring the local vector DC magnetic field in Earth’s polar magnetosphere; dual triaxial boom-mounted fluxgate sensors, outboard and inboard for spacecraft-field removal, provide redundant measurements over selectable ranges of about ±700, ±5700, and ±47,000 nT.

Polar UVI (Ultraviolet Imager) ultraviolet auroral imager measuring global auroral emissions, morphology, total energy influx, and characteristic energy of precipitating particles; uses a VUV (vacuum ultraviolet) channel at six selected wavelengths from 120.0-180.0 nm and a NUV (near ultraviolet) channel at five selected wavelengths from 247.0-337.1 nm with ~60 s imaging cadence

Polar VIS (Visible Imaging System) imager measuring nighttime auroral and airglow emissions at visible wavelengths; comprising HRC (High Resolution Camera), LRC (Low Resolution Camera), and EC (Earth Camera), a far-ultraviolet 124–149 nm pointing imager, with VIS filters for N2+ 391.4 nm, O I 557.7/630.0 nm, H I 656.3 nm, and O II 732.0 nm emissions.

Parker Solar Probe Ephemeris (spacecraft ephemeris) platform support data product giving PSP spacecraft position and velocity for heliophysics analysis, including heliocentric distance, solar longitude/latitude, Sun-spacecraft geometry, and coordinate-frame quantities such as RTN or inertial state vectors used to contextualize in situ fields and particles measurements

Parker Solar Probe MAG (Magnetometer) dual triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector magnetic field in the solar corona and solar wind; one of the FIELDS (Fields Experiment) suite sensors alongside SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), RFS (Radio Frequency Spectrometer), DFB (Digital Fields Board) and V1-V5 electric antennas, with inner MAGi and outer MAGo sensors sampling to ~293 Sa/s, ~140 Hz bandwidth, ranges ±1024 to ±65,536 nT

Parker Solar Probe SPC (Solar Probe Cup) Faraday cup measuring sunward solar-wind ion and electron reduced distribution functions, fluxes, and flow angles versus energy per charge; one of the SWEAP (Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons) suite sensors alongside SPAN-A (Solar Probe Analyzer A) and SPAN-B (Solar Probe Analyzer B), with ~60° field of view and ranges ~50 eV/q-8 keV/q for ions and ~50 eV-2 keV for electrons

Parker Solar Probe DFB (Digital Fields Board) waveform and spectral receiver measuring low-frequency electric and magnetic-field fluctuations for the FIELDS electric and magnetic fields suite, alongside MAG fluxgate magnetometers, SCM (Search-Coil Magnetometer), RFS (Radio Frequency Spectrometer), and V1-V5 voltage probes; digitizes five voltage-sensor and four SCM channels from DC to ~60 kHz.

Parker Solar Probe V1 (Voltage Probe 1) antenna measuring single-ended electric potential for FIELDS electric-field, plasma-wave and radio measurements; one of the five FIELDS voltage probes alongside V2, V3, V4 and boom-mounted V5, paired with the other sunlit whip probes to form double-probe DC/AC electric-field channels

Parker Solar Probe V2 (Voltage Probe 2) antenna measuring spacecraft-to-plasma potential, electric-field components, plasma waves, and radio-frequency voltage signals for the FIELDS suite; one of five voltage probes alongside V1, V3, V4 sunlit electric antennas and the boom-mounted V5 sensor, used with MAG and SCM magnetic-field sensors

Parker Solar Probe V3 (Voltage Probe 3) electric-field antenna measuring spacecraft-to-probe potential and contributing to DC/AC electric-field, quasi-thermal-noise, and radio/plasma-wave observations; one of the FIELDS (Fields Experiment) voltage sensors alongside V1, V2, V4 sunlit probes and the V5 boom-mounted probe

Parker Solar Probe FIELDS (Fields Experiment) V4 (Voltage Probe 4) voltage-probe antenna measuring electric potential, DC/low-frequency electric fields, and radio/plasma waves; one of the five FIELDS electric antennas alongside V1, V2, V3, and V5, with V4 one of the four sunlit heat-shield-mounted probes used for double-probe and capacitive wave measurements

Parker Solar Probe SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) search-coil magnetometer measuring three-component AC magnetic-field fluctuations and plasma waves from 10 Hz-50 kHz plus one LF/MF component from 1 kHz-1 MHz; a FIELDS suite sensor alongside the MAG fluxgate magnetometers, RFS radio receivers, TDS waveform sampler, DFB spectral processor, and electric-field antennas

Parker Solar Probe V5 (Voltage Probe 5) antenna measuring single-ended electric potential and plasma/radio wave voltage in the FIELDS suite; a boom-mounted umbra voltage sensor complementing the sunlit V1-V4 electric-field antennas, MAGi/MAGo fluxgate magnetometers, SCM search-coil magnetometer, RFS radio-frequency spectrometer, and DFB digital fields board

Parker Solar Probe FIELDS (Electromagnetic Fields Investigation) fields-and-waves suite measuring DC magnetic/electric fields, plasma waves, spacecraft potential/plasma density and solar radio bursts; comprising V1-V4 sunlit and V5 axial voltage probes, MAGi/MAGo triaxial fluxgate magnetometers, SCM (search-coil magnetometer; 10 Hz-1 MHz), and RFS (Radio Frequency Spectrometer) LFR (low-frequency receiver) and HFR (high-frequency receiver) channels to ~19 MHz

Parker Solar Probe TDS (Time Domain Sampler) waveform receiver measuring burst electric- and magnetic-field waveforms for the FIELDS suite, one of the FIELDS processors alongside DFB (Digital Fields Board), RFS (Radio Frequency Spectrometer), MAG (fluxgate magnetometers) and SCM (search-coil magnetometer); samples five channels from electric antennas V1-V5 and one SCM axis at up to 1.92 MSa/s, ~1 MHz Nyquist

Parker Solar Probe SWEAP (Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons) electrostatic-analyzer/Faraday-cup suite measuring solar-wind proton, alpha, heavy-ion, and electron distributions, moments, and flow angles; comprising SPC (Solar Probe Cup; ions 50 eV/q-8 keV/q, electrons 50 eV-2 keV), SPAN-Ai (Solar Probe Analyzer ram ion, few eV/q-20 keV/q with time-of-flight), SPAN-Ae, and SPAN-B electron analyzers (few eV-20 keV)

Parker Solar Probe RFS/HFR (Radio Frequency Spectrometer High Frequency Receiver) spectral power receiver measuring high-frequency electric-field spectra and solar radio emissions from ~1.3 to 19.2 MHz; one of the FIELDS suite RFS receivers alongside LFR, using V1-V4 antenna dipole/monopole inputs to produce auto- and cross-spectra for remote radio sensing

Parker Solar Probe LFR (Low Frequency Receiver) spectral power receiver measuring electric-field plasma-wave and quasi-thermal-noise spectra from ~10 kHz to 2.4 MHz; the low-frequency channel of the FIELDS Radio Frequency Spectrometer (RFS) alongside HFR (High Frequency Receiver), using V1-V4 antenna inputs and cross-spectral measurements

Parker Solar Probe HET (High Energy Telescope) double-ended energetic particle telescope measuring high-energy solar energetic electrons (~0.5-6 MeV) and ions, including protons and He (~10-100 MeV/nucleon, heavier ions to higher energies); the high-energy EPI-Hi sensor in the ISʘIS suite alongside LET1 and LET2, with HET-A/HET-B viewing apertures

Parker Solar Probe LET1 (Low Energy Telescope 1) double-ended energetic particle telescope measuring solar energetic ion composition, spectra, and angular distributions in the low-MeV range, roughly ~1–20 MeV/nucleon for H–heavy ions and sub- to few-MeV electrons; one of the three EPI-Hi (Energetic Particle Instrument-High) telescopes in ISʘIS (Integrated Science Investigation of the Sun) alongside HET (High Energy Telescope) and LET2 (Low Energy Telescope 2)"

Parker Solar Probe LET2 (Low Energy Telescope 2) energetic particle telescope measuring near-Sun solar energetic protons, helium and heavier ions (~1-15 MeV/nucleon, species dependent) and MeV electrons; the single-ended low-energy telescope of EPI-Hi (Energetic Particle Instrument-High) in ISʘIS (Integrated Science Investigation of the Sun), alongside LET1 and HET (High Energy Telescope)

Parker Solar Probe EPI-Lo (Energetic Particle Instrument-Low) time-of-flight energetic-particle mass spectrometer measuring directional spectra and composition in the ISʘIS (Integrated Science Investigation of the Sun) suite alongside EPI-Hi (Energetic Particle Instrument-High): electrons ~25-1000 keV, protons ~0.04-7 MeV, and heavy ions ~0.02-2 MeV/nuc, resolving ³He/⁴He and major ion species over many look directions

Parker Solar Probe SPAN-A (Solar Probe Analyzer A; houses the ram-side ion analyzer SPAN-Ai, also designated SPAN-I or SPAN-Ion (Livi et al. 2022), and the ram-side electron analyzer SPAN-Ae) electrostatic analyzer pair measuring ram-side ion and electron velocity distributions; one of the SWEAP (Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons) suite sensors alongside the SPC (Solar Probe Cup) and SPAN-B (Solar Probe Analyzer B), with ions from several eV/q to 20 keV/q using time-of-flight mass/charge discrimination and electrons from several eV to 20 keV

Parker Solar Probe SPAN-B (Solar Probe Analyzer B) electrostatic analyzer measuring anti-ram solar-wind electron velocity distributions from several eV to 20 keV; the electron-only sensor of the SWEAP (Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons) suite alongside SPC (Solar Probe Cup) and SPAN-A (Solar Probe Analyzer A); together with SPAN-A's electron analyzer SPAN-Ae it constitutes the SPAN electron measurement, also designated SPAN-E or SPAN-Electron (Whittlesey et al. 2020), paired with SPAN-A electron coverage for near-4π electron fields of view excluding the heat shield.

RBSP-A RBSPICE (Radiation Belt Storm Probes Ion Composition Experiment) energetic particle spectrometer measuring ring-current ion composition, pitch-angle and energy spectra, and pressure distributions; the Puck sensor resolves H+, He+, and O+ ions from tens of keV to ~1 MeV and electrons from ~25 keV to ~1 MeV with ~22.5° angular bins and ΔE/E~0.1

RBSP-A (Radiation Belt Storm Probe A) Ephemeris spacecraft ephemeris/platform data product measuring the Van Allen Probe A spacecraft position and orbit context in geocentric coordinate systems, including position vectors commonly used for radiation-belt studies such as GEO, GSE, GSM, SM, and magnetic coordinates for conjunction and mapping analyses

RBSP-A EMFISIS (Electric and Magnetic Field Instrument Suite and Integrated Science) waveform and field suite measuring DC magnetic fields, plasma waves, wave spectra, wave normals, Poynting flux, and upper-hybrid density; comprising MAG (tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer, DC-15 Hz) and WAVES with search-coil magnetic fields 10 Hz-12 kHz, spin-plane electric fields 10 Hz-12 kHz, and single-channel electric fields 10-400 kHz.

RBSP-B RBSPICE (Radiation Belt Storm Probes Ion Composition Experiment) energetic-particle spectrometer measuring ring-current and radiation-belt ion composition, spectra, pressure and pitch-angle distributions; its Puck time-of-flight/solid-state sensor resolves H+, He+ and O+ ions from ~40 keV to ~1 MeV and electrons from ~25 keV to ~1 MeV.

RBSP-B Ephemeris (Radiation Belt Storm Probe B spacecraft positions) platform/ancillary data product measuring the Van Allen Probe B spacecraft location and state vector for orbit context, reported in geocentric coordinate systems such as geographic/geocentric, Geocentric Solar Ecliptic, Geocentric Solar Magnetospheric, and Solar Magnetic coordinates

RBSP-B EMFISIS (Electric and Magnetic Field Instrument Suite and Integrated Science) waveform receiver and magnetometer suite measuring ambient magnetic fields, plasma waves, and electron density; comprising MAG (fluxgate magnetometer, quasi-static vector B to 15 Hz), WFR (Waveform Receiver, 10 Hz-12 kHz electric and magnetic spectra/spectral matrices), and HFR (High Frequency Receiver, 10-400 kHz electric spectra including upper-hybrid resonance)

RBSP-A EFW (Electric Field and Waves) electric-field and plasma-wave suite measuring three-dimensional electric fields from quasi-static to >500 kHz, spin-plane and spin-axis convection fields to 12 Hz, spacecraft potential for cold plasma density (~0.1-100 cm-3), and electric/magnetic wave spectra, cross spectra, and burst waveforms around 1 Hz-12 kHz.

RBSP-A RPS (Relativistic Proton Spectrometer) energetic particle telescope measuring trapped inner Van Allen belt proton fluxes, spectra, and pitch-angle distributions from 50 MeV to 2 GeV, extending Radiation Belt Storm Probes coverage above ~150 MeV for radiation-belt dose, displacement-damage, and specification-model studies

RBSP-A ECT (Energetic Particle, Composition, and Thermal Plasma) energetic particle and plasma spectrometer suite measuring radiation-belt electron and ion composition, spectra, and pitch-angle distributions from ~1 eV to relativistic energies; comprising HOPE (Helium Oxygen Proton Electron), MagEIS (Magnetic Electron Ion Spectrometer), and REPT (Relativistic Electron-Proton Telescope) sensors

RBSP-B (Radiation Belt Storm Probe B, Van Allen Probe B) EFW (Electric Field and Waves) fields-and-waves suite measuring three-component quasi-static electric fields, spacecraft potential/cold plasma density, and electric and magnetic wave spectra/waveforms in the inner magnetosphere, using spin-plane and spin-axis double-probe sensors: continuous fields to 12 Hz, spectra ~1 Hz-12 kHz, burst waveforms to >500 kHz.

Radiation Belt Storm Probes B (RBSP-B) RPS (Relativistic Proton Spectrometer) energetic-particle telescope measuring trapped inner Van Allen belt protons from 50 MeV to 2 GeV, with silicon-stack channels to ~400 MeV and Cherenkov response above ~400 MeV for radiation-belt flux, dose, displacement-damage, and model-validation studies.

RBSP-B ECT (Energetic Particle, Composition, and Thermal Plasma Suite) energetic particle suite measuring inner-magnetospheric electrons and ions, composition, spectra, pitch-angle distributions, and radiation-belt dynamics from ~1 eV to tens of MeV; comprising HOPE (Helium Oxygen Proton Electron), MagEIS (Magnetic Electron Ion Spectrometer), and REPT (Relativistic Electron Proton Telescope)

Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 COWBOY (COrnell Wire BOom Yo-yo) long-wire electric-field boom instrument measuring direct-current electric fields and HF (high frequency) and VLF (very low frequency) electric-field waves on the RENU 2 NASA sounding-rocket payload launched from Andøya into the dayside cusp on 13 Dec 2015.
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: RENU 2 EPLAS (Electron Plasma) top-hat electrostatic analyzer measuring precipitating auroral/cusp electron differential energy spectra, pitch-angle distributions, and energy flux from 10 eV to 15 keV at 1 ms cadence, with 360° field of view and 10° angular resolution on the Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 sounding-rocket flight from Andøya into the dayside cusp on 13 Dec 2015
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: RENU 2 (Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2) ERPA (Electron Retarding Potential Analyzer) electrostatic retarding-potential analyzer measuring thermal electron current-voltage distributions from 0 to 3 eV in 0.06 eV steps on the 13 Dec 2015 Andøya dayside-cusp sounding-rocket payload for neutral-upwelling studies
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 (RENU 2) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) sounding-rocket magnetometer measuring vector magnetic-field strength and direction along the 13 December 2015 Andøya dayside-cusp trajectory, providing in situ magnetic perturbations for cusp electrodynamics and neutral-upwelling studies
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: RENU 2 (Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2) IG2 (Ion Gauge 2) ion-gauge package measuring neutral particle density, primarily atomic oxygen number density, along the NASA dayside-cusp sounding-rocket trajectory from Andøya on 13 Dec 2015; comprising six Aerospace-provided Anelva ion gauges on the RENU 2 payload
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 PMT (Photomultiplier Tubes) photometer set measuring auroral optical emission intensity on the RENU 2 dayside-cusp sounding-rocket payload launched from Andøya in 2015; three narrowband PMT channels observe the atomic oxygen OI 557.7 nm green line and OI 630.0 nm red line
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2 UVPMT (Ultraviolet Photomultiplier Tube) photomultiplier-tube photometer measuring far-ultraviolet airglow with peak response at atomic oxygen 130.4 nm, flown on the RENU 2 sounding-rocket payload into the dayside cusp from Andøya on 13 Dec 2015 to diagnose neutral upwelling/thermospheric response
mission_name: Rocket Experiment for Neutral Upwelling 2, RENU 2, Sounding Rocket Payload

description: Rosetta Ephemeris spacecraft trajectory and position data product reporting the Rosetta orbiter location and velocity versus time, used to determine heliocentric, cometocentric, and planetary context for measurements near comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko and during interplanetary cruise/flybys

ROCSAT-1 (Republic of China Satellite-1) IPEI (Ionospheric Plasma and Electrodynamics Instrument) ionospheric plasma diagnostics suite measuring ion density, temperature, and vector drift velocity in the low-latitude/equatorial topside ionosphere; comprising IT (ion trap), dual IDM (ion drift meter) sensors, and RPA (retarding potential analyzer) for plasma structure, bubbles, and electrodynamics studies

Sakigake Ephemeris (Sakigake Positions) platform trajectory data product measuring spacecraft position and velocity rather than fields or particles, used to locate the Japanese Sakigake interplanetary/Halley probe in geocentric and heliocentric coordinates for solar-wind, comet Halley, and interplanetary context studies.

SESAME AIS (Advanced Ionospheric Sounder) high-frequency dynasonde/radar sounder measuring ionospheric echo time of flight, amplitude, and phase versus frequency and time over 0.1–30 MHz, with ~1–3° phase accuracy; used to diagnose electron-density structure, auroral arcs, and localized energetic-particle precipitation

SESAME (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements) FPI (Fabry-Perot Interferometer) ground-based optical interferometer measuring Doppler shifts and line widths of atomic oxygen airglow/auroral emissions, especially O I 630.0 nm, to derive thermospheric neutral winds and temperatures while scanning cardinal look directions at ~30° elevation.

SESAME (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic MEasurements) MAG (Magnetometer) fluxgate magnetometer measuring the terrestrial magnetic-field H, D, and Z components for coordinated Antarctic geospace studies, with 1 s sampling cadence and approximately 1 nT field resolution.

SESAME (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements) RIO (relative ionospheric opacity meter) riometer measuring ionospheric absorption of cosmic radio noise in dB; reports north, east, south, and west look directions transformed to an L-shell-aligned coordinate system at 1 s cadence with ~0.1 dB sensitivity

SESAME VELOX (Satellite Experiments Simultaneous with Antarctic Measurements VLF/ELF Logger Experiment) 10-channel very-low-frequency/extremely-low-frequency waveform receiver measuring magnetospheric radio waves from 0.5-30 kHz, used for whistler-mode propagation, wave-particle interactions, wave-induced precipitation, and plasma structure studies with typical 1 min recordings every 15 min

Student Nitric Oxide Explorer (SNOE) UVS (Ultraviolet Spectrometer) ultraviolet limb spectrometer measuring thermospheric nitric oxide (NO) density from NO gamma bands, with two 3.7 nm-bandpass channels centered on the (1,0) band at 215 nm and the (0,1) band at 237 nm, providing limb altitude profiles with ~3.5 km vertical resolution and 27 ms integrations.

SOHO Positions (Solar and Heliospheric Observatory ephemeris) platform ephemeris data product providing spacecraft time, position, and velocity for the SOHO halo orbit about the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point in heliocentric and geocentric coordinates; ancillary trajectory information for observation geometry, not a particle, field, or photon detector

Solar Orbiter Ephemeris virtual platform product providing spacecraft position and velocity, trajectory, heliocentric distance, heliographic latitude/longitude, and observing geometry for the Solar Orbiter spacecraft; used to contextualize in situ and remote-sensing measurements rather than a physical sensor.

ST5-094 Ephemeris (Space Technology 5 spacecraft 094 ephemeris) platform/trajectory data product giving spacecraft position and orbit state vectors in heliophysics coordinate systems such as geocentric, GSE, GSM, and SM; unit 094 of the 2006 ST5 three-microsatellite magnetospheric technology-demonstration constellation.

ST5-155 ST5 (Space Technology 5) ephemeris/position platform product providing spacecraft trajectory, position, and orbit coordinates for the ST5-155 microsatellite, one of the three 2006 ST5 technology-demonstration spacecraft, used for location context of in situ measurements rather than as a separate fields or particle sensor

ST5-224 Ephemeris (Space Technology 5 spacecraft 224 ephemeris) platform position data product specifying the ST5-224 observatory trajectory and location in geocentric coordinate systems, used to contextualize ST5 magnetometer observations by orbit position, altitude, latitude/longitude, magnetic coordinates, and local time rather than measuring a plasma or field quantity

STEREO-A (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Ahead) Ephemeris platform/ancillary data product reporting the spacecraft trajectory and position vectors in multiple heliocentric, geocentric, and mission coordinate systems, used to locate STEREO-A for contextual analysis of in-situ fields/particles and remote solar observations

STEREO-A IMPACT (In situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) particle-and-field suite measuring the interplanetary magnetic field, solar-wind electrons, and suprathermal/energetic particles; comprising MAG (Magnetometer), SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer, <1 eV to several keV electrons), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope, ~2-20 keV electrons), SEPT (Solar Electron Proton Telescope, 20-400 keV electrons and 20 keV-7 MeV protons), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope, He-Fe ions at 30 keV/n-2 MeV/n), LET (Low Energy Telescope, 1.5-30 MeV/n ions), and HET (High Energy Telescope, ions to ~100 MeV/n and electrons to ~5 MeV)

STEREO-A PLASTIC (PLAsma and SupraThermal Ion Composition) time-of-flight electrostatic analyzer measuring solar-wind and suprathermal ion composition, M and M/q, energy spectra, and arrival direction over ~0.3-80 keV/q; key cited channels are the SWS Small Channel for H+ and He++, SWS Main Channel for heavy ions (C, O, Mg, Si, Fe), and Wide Angle Partition for pickup/local ions including He+ <40 keV/q

STEREO-A IMPACT/HET (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients/High Energy Telescope) particle telescope measuring solar energetic protons (~13-100 MeV), helium (~14-100 MeV/nucleon) and electrons (~0.7-6 MeV); IMPACT sibling sensors are MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (solar wind electron analyzer), STE (suprathermal electron), SEPT (solar electron proton telescope), SIT (suprathermal ion telescope) and LET (low energy telescope)

STEREO-A (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory Ahead) IMPACT/MAG (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients Magnetometer) tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the DC interplanetary magnetic-field vector on the boom, with auto-ranging sensitivity for low solar-wind fields up to near-Earth commissioning fields; one IMPACT sensor alongside SWEA, STE, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET.

STEREO-A (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Ahead) STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope), an IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) energetic-particle telescope measuring ~2-20 keV suprathermal electrons in two oppositely directed Parker-spiral views, alongside MAG, SWEA, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET for solar-wind, flare, shock, and interplanetary CME studies

STEREO-A (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Ahead) IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients)/SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer) top-hat electrostatic analyzer measuring solar wind core, halo, and strahl electron distribution functions and pitch-angle distributions from <1 eV to several keV with near-4π angular coverage, alongside IMPACT MAG, STE, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET

STEREO-A SWAVES (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory/WAVES) radio and plasma wave instrument measuring solar type II/III radio bursts, source direction/size, and in situ electric-field plasma waves/waveforms from ~2.5 kHz to 16 MHz; comprising HFR (High Frequency Receiver), LFR (Low Frequency Receiver), FFR (Fixed Frequency Receiver, 10-40 kHz) and TDS (Time Domain Sampler), using three orthogonal 6 m monopole antennas

STEREO-A LET (Low Energy Telescope) particle detector measuring solar energetic H-Ni ions at ~3-30 MeV/n, including 3He and trans-iron nuclei Z=30-83, with composition, spectra, angular distributions, and timing; one of four IMPACT SEP sensors alongside SEPT, SIT, and HET.

STEREO-A IMPACT/SEPT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients/Solar Electron Proton Telescope) particle telescope measuring 20–400 keV electrons and 20 keV–7 MeV protons; one IMPACT sensor alongside MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (solar wind electron analyzer), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope) and HET (High Energy Telescope), with SEPT-E and SEPT-N/S look directions for anisotropy

STEREO-A SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope) time-of-flight ion mass spectrometer in IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) measuring elemental composition and spectra of suprathermal He-Fe ions from 30 keV/n to 2 MeV/n; energetic-particle sibling to SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), and HET (High Energy Telescope)

STEREO-B Ephemeris (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory Behind spacecraft position) platform ephemeris data product measuring spacecraft position, velocity, heliocentric distance, heliographic/HEE/HEEQ longitude-latitude, and Earth-Sun-spacecraft separation in common heliophysics coordinate systems for the STEREO-B context.

STEREO-B (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory Behind) IMPACT (In situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) particles-and-fields suite measuring interplanetary magnetic-field vectors, solar-wind/suprathermal electrons, and energetic particle fluxes/composition; comprising MAG (magnetometer), SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer, <1 eV-several keV electrons), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope, ~2-20 keV electrons), SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope, 20-400 keV electrons and 20 keV-7 MeV protons), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope, He-Fe ions 30 keV/n-2 MeV/n), LET (Low Energy Telescope, 1.5-13 MeV/n hydrogen/helium and 2-30 MeV/n heavy ions), and HET (High Energy Telescope, hydrogen/helium to ~100 MeV/n and electrons to ~5 MeV).

STEREO-B IMPACT/HET (Solar TErrestrial RElations Observatory-B In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients/High Energy Telescope) particle telescope measuring solar energetic protons and helium nuclei from ~13 to >100 MeV/nucleon and electrons to ~5–6 MeV, one IMPACT sensor alongside LET (Low Energy Telescope), SIT, SEPT, STE, SWEA, and MAG.

STEREO-B IMPACT/MAG (Solar Terrestrial Relations Observatory-B In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring vector interplanetary magnetic-field strength/direction (up to ~8 vectors/s, auto-ranging); one suite sensor alongside SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer), STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope), SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope), and SIT/LET/HET (Suprathermal Ion, Low Energy and High Energy Telescopes)

STEREO-B STE (Suprathermal Electron Telescope) energetic particle instrument measuring ~2-20 keV solar-wind superhalo and flare/shock-accelerated electrons for heliospheric field-line tracing; one of the IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) suite sensors alongside MAG, SWEA, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET.

STEREO-B SWEA (Solar Wind Electron Analyzer) particle detector measuring solar-wind core, halo, and strahl electron distribution functions and pitch-angle spectra from <1 eV to ~3 keV; one of the IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients) suite sensors alongside MAG, STE, SEPT, SIT, LET, and HET

STEREO-B PLASTIC (Plasma and SupraThermal Ion Composition) ion composition mass spectrometer measuring solar-wind and suprathermal ion energy spectra, direction, mass and M/q from ~0.3–80 keV/q; includes SWS Small Channel for H+ and He++, SWS Main Channel for heavy solar-wind ions C, O, Mg, Si and Fe, and the Wide Angle Partition for H+, He++, He+ and pickup He+ (<40 keV/q)

STEREO-B SWAVES (STEREO/WAVES) radio and plasma wave instrument measuring solar Type II/III radio bursts, source direction/size, in-situ Langmuir/plasma waves and electric-field waveforms from ~2.5 kHz to 16 MHz; comprising the HFR (High Frequency Receiver), LFR (Low Frequency Receiver), FFR (Fixed Frequency Receiver) and TDS (Time Domain Sampler) using three orthogonal 6 m monopoles

STEREO-B LET (Low Energy Telescope), a solid-state particle telescope in the IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients) Solar Energetic Particle suite alongside SEPT (Solar Electron Proton Telescope), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope), and HET (High Energy Telescope), measuring H–Ni ions at ~3–30 MeV/n, including 3He and trans-iron nuclei (30≤Z≤83)

STEREO-B SEPT (Solar Electron and Proton Telescope) particle telescope of IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and Coronal Mass Ejection Transients) measuring electrons (~30-400 keV) and protons/ions (~60 keV-7 MeV); sibling energetic-particle sensors include STE (Suprathermal Electron), SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope) and HET (High Energy Telescope), with SEPT-E and SEPT-N/S magnet/foil views along/against the Parker spiral and north/south of the ecliptic

STEREO-B SIT (Suprathermal Ion Telescope) time-of-flight ion mass spectrometer in IMPACT (In-situ Measurements of Particles and CME Transients) measuring He-Fe suprathermal ion composition and spectra from ~30 keV/n to 2 MeV/n; energetic-particle sensor alongside SEPT, LET, and HET, with a 17°×44° field of view for solar energetic particle, CME-shock, and CIR ions

Suisei Ephemeris (spacecraft position ephemeris) ancillary platform data product measuring/recording Suisei spacecraft position, velocity, and trajectory versus time for locating Planet-A/Suisei observations in heliocentric or geocentric coordinates, especially during interplanetary cruise and the Halley comet encounter

SAMPEX (Solar, Anomalous, and Magnetospheric Particle Explorer) MAST (Mass Spectrometer Telescope) solid-state energetic-particle telescope measuring isotopic composition and energy spectra of energetic nuclei from lithium through nickel (Z=3-28) at ~10 to several hundred MeV/nucleon with ~0.2 amu mass resolution, complementing LICA (Low Energy Ion Composition Analyzer), HILT (Heavy Ion Large Telescope), and PET (Proton/Electron Telescope)

SAMPEX HILT (Heavy Ion Large Telescope) energetic-particle telescope measuring charge, energy, mass, and species-resolved fluxes of heavy ions and cosmic rays; one of four SAMPEX particle instruments alongside LICA, MAST, and PET, covering ~8-310 MeV/nucleon overall, including He 3.9-90, C 7.2-160, O 8.3-310, Ne 9.1-250, and Fe 11-90 MeV/nucleon

SAMPEX (Solar Anomalous and Magnetospheric Particle Explorer) PET (Proton-Electron Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring magnetospheric and solar energetic electrons from 1-30 MeV, including >0.4 MeV high-rate precipitating-electron counts, protons and helium from 18-85 MeV/nucleon (trackable to several hundred MeV/nucleon), and heavier nuclei from 54-195 MeV/nucleon

SAMPEX LICA (Low-Energy Ion Composition Analyzer) energetic ion composition telescope measuring solar and magnetospheric ions from ~0.5–5 MeV/nucleon, with zenith-viewing mass/isotope separation for He through Ni and rates for H, He, O, Si-group, and Fe-group ions; flown alongside HILT, MAST, and PET on SAMPEX

THEMIS-A (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) Ephemeris platform/status data product providing probe A/THA spacecraft position and velocity, geocentric solar ecliptic and geocentric solar magnetospheric coordinates, orbital location, attitude, spin-phase context, and ancillary status for interpreting THEMIS-A field and particle measurements

THEMIS-A EFI (Electric Field Instrument) double-sphere probe measuring the ambient vector electric field, differential probe potentials E12/E34/E56, individual V1-V6 potentials, spacecraft floating potential, and sub-spin plasma density; six probes on spin-plane and axial booms provide DC waveforms to 4 kHz, AC-coupled fields ~10 Hz-8 kHz, spectra, and 100-400 kHz integrated wave power

THEMIS-A ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) electrostatic analyzer pair measuring thermal electron and ion fluxes, full 3-D velocity distributions, density, bulk velocity, and temperature from ~3 eV to 30 keV, comprising separate electron ESA and ion ESA sensors on the THEMIS-A spacecraft in the THEMIS constellation

THEMIS-A SCM (Search Coil Magnetometer) triaxial induction-coil magnetometer measuring AC magnetic-field fluctuations and wave magnetic spectra from ~0.1 Hz to 4 kHz, extending to ~8 kHz in wave-burst data; a THEMIS fields/waves sensor used with EFI, FGM, and DFB products, including SCM waveform, filter-bank, and FFT spectral channels.

THEMIS-A (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms probe A) FGM (Fluxgate Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer measuring the DC vector magnetic field and low-frequency fluctuations to 64 Hz with ~0.01 nT sensitivity; data products include FGL low-rate survey, FGH 128 sps burst, and FGS spin-fit magnetic field in DSL, GSE, and GSM coordinates

THEMIS-A (Time History of Events and Macroscale Interactions during Substorms) SST (Solid State Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring superthermal electron and ion directional flux/energy-flux spectrograms with two sensor heads sweeping most of the sky; primary ranges are ions 30-300 keV and electrons 30-100 keV, with extended capability ~20 keV-6 MeV ions and ~25 keV-1 MeV electrons.

THEMIS-A MOM (On Board Moments) onboard plasma moments product measuring ion and electron density, number/energy flux, bulk velocity, pressure, temperature, and six-component momentum flux tensor from combined ESA (Electrostatic Analyzer) and SST (Solid State Telescope) particle data, corrected with EFI (Electric Field Instrument) spacecraft potential, with spin-resolution outputs in DSL (Despun Sun–L-vector), GSE, GSM, and MFA coordinates

TWINS 1 (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) spacecraft ephemeris/position platform data providing the location of the TWINS-1 hosted payload in its high-inclination Molniya orbit, used to determine viewing geometry and context for TWINS ENA imaging and Lyman-alpha observations; distinct from TWINS-2 positions.

TWINS-1 ENA (Energetic Neutral Atom) imager measuring global magnetospheric charge-exchange neutral hydrogen fluxes and ring-current ion distributions at ~1-100 keV; the TWINS-1 unit of the Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers mission package comprises dual wide-angle ENA sensor heads and an LAD (Lyman-alpha Detector) for geocoronal H density correction

TWINS 1 LAD (Lyman-alpha Detector) ultraviolet photometric imager measuring resonantly scattered H Lyman-alpha emission at 121.6 nm from neutral hydrogen in the terrestrial exosphere/geocorona; two independent sensors on the rotating actuator view ±40° from the spin axis with 4° FWHM fields of view, providing 360° azimuth coverage at 60 s cadence

TWINS-2 ENA (Energetic Neutral Atom) imager measuring charge-exchange neutral atom images of magnetospheric ion populations at ~1–100 keV; the second TWINS (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) flight unit, with paired wide-angle ENA sensor heads and a companion Lyman-alpha detector for geocoronal neutral hydrogen correction, identical to TWINS-1

TWINS-2 (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers 2) LAD (Lyman-alpha Detector) ultraviolet photometer/imager measuring 121.6 nm hydrogen Lyman-alpha emission from neutral geocoronal H, using two independent narrowband sensors pointed ±40° from the actuator spin axis with ~4° fields of view, 360° azimuthal scan coverage, and 60 s cadence

TWINS-2 (Two Wide-angle Imaging Neutral-atom Spectrometers) Ephemeris platform position product measuring spacecraft location, velocity, and orbit geometry versus time for the second TWINS spacecraft, used to geolocate energetic neutral atom images and provide viewing/context coordinates rather than particle or field measurements.

Ulysses Ephemeris spacecraft trajectory/position platform data product providing the Ulysses spacecraft location and motion for heliophysics context, including heliocentric distance, heliographic latitude and longitude, and position/velocity vectors used to place plasma, field, energetic-particle, and radio measurements along the out-of-ecliptic solar polar orbit

Ulysses magnetic field investigation (HED/VHM/FGM), combining a triaxial fluxgate magnetometer (FGM) and a vector helium magnetometer (VHM) to measure interplanetary magnetic field strength and direction in the inner heliosphere, including over the Sun's poles at high solar latitudes

Ulysses SWOOPS (Solar Wind Observations Over the Poles of the Sun) electrostatic analyzer plasma instrument measuring solar wind ion and electron velocity distributions, density, speed, temperature, and proton/alpha bulk parameters; comprising an electron analyzer (1-900 eV) and a solar wind ion analyzer (257 eV-35 keV/q) for heliospheric and Jovian plasma studies

Ulysses SWICS (Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer) solar-wind ion composition/time-of-flight mass spectrometer measuring elemental and ionic charge-state composition, temperatures and bulk speeds of ions H through Fe, plus pickup and suprathermal ions, over 110 eV/q-66.7 keV/q and solar-wind speeds 145-1350 km/s.

Ulysses AT (Anisotropy Telescopes) energetic particle telescope measuring ~0.7–7 MeV/n proton and helium intensities and three-dimensional anisotropies; one of the COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensors alongside HET (High Energy Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), KET (Kiel Electron Telescope), and HFT (High Flux Telescope)

Ulysses HET (High Energy Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays, including H through Fe ions at ~6–600 MeV/n and electron channels at a few–tens of MeV; one of the Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation suite sensors alongside LET (Low Energy Telescope), KET (Kiel Electron Telescope), HFT (High Flux Telescope), and AT (Anisotropy Telescope).

Ulysses HFT (High Flux Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring high-flux solar energetic particles, especially ~0.3-7 MeV protons and ~0.4-4 MeV/nucleon helium; a small-aperture COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensor alongside HET (High Energy Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), KET (Kiel Electron Telescope), and AT (Anisotropy Telescope).

Ulysses KET (Kiel Electron Telescope) energetic particle telescope measuring high-energy electrons (~3-200 MeV) and protons and helium nuclei (~3-2100 MeV/nucleon) with dE/dx-E and Cherenkov particle identification; one of the COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensors alongside HET (High Energy Telescope), LET (Low Energy Telescope), ATs (Anisotropy Telescopes), and HFT (High Flux Telescope)

Ulysses LET (Low Energy Telescope) energetic-particle telescope measuring solar energetic particle and cosmic-ray ions—protons, helium, and heavier nuclei—at ~1–20 MeV/nucleon with dE/dx–E pulse-height analysis; one of the five COSPIN (Cosmic Ray and Solar Particle Investigation) suite sensors alongside AT (Anisotropy Telescope), HET (High Energy Telescope), HFT (High Flux Telescope), and KET (Kiel Electron Telescope)

Ulysses URAP (Unified Radio and Plasma Waves) radio and plasma-wave investigation measuring solar/Jovian radio emissions, Langmuir/plasma waves, waveforms, and electron density from DC to 1 MHz; comprising RAR (Radio Astronomy Receiver, 1.25-940 kHz), PFR (Plasma Frequency Receiver, 0.57-35 kHz), FES (Fast Envelope Sampler, 10 Hz-60 kHz), WFA (Wave Form Analyzer, DC-500 Hz), and an active sounder

Ulysses EPAC (Energetic Particle Composition) energetic-particle telescope experiment measuring composition, spectra, angular distributions, and anisotropies of interplanetary ions and electrons; four spin-scanned telescopes resolve H, He, and heavy nuclei to Fe over ~0.5-1.5 MeV protons, 0.1-0.5 MeV/nucleon Z≥1 ions, 0.4-4 MeV/nucleon heavy ions, and electron channels at 0.1-0.4 and >0.3 MeV

Ulysses HISCALE (Heliosphere Instrument for Spectra, Composition and Anisotropy at Low Energies) energetic particle instrument measuring electron and ion spectra, anisotropies and composition; comprising LEFS60/LEFS150 (Low Energy Foil Spectrometers), LEMS30/LEMS120 (Low Energy Magnetic Spectrometers) and CA60 (Composition Aperture), covering electrons ~30-300 keV, ions ~50 keV-5 MeV and nuclei ~1-15 MeV/nucleon

Voyager 1/2 PWS (Plasma Wave System) waveform and spectrum receiver measuring electric-field plasma waves, Langmuir waves, whistlers, and radio-frequency wave activity in planetary magnetospheres and the solar wind; includes a 16-channel step-frequency spectrum analyzer and low-frequency waveform receiver covering 10 Hz-56 kHz, deriving electron density from plasma-wave emissions via shared 10-m electric antennas

Voyager 2 PWS (Plasma Wave System) waveform and 16-channel step-frequency receiver measuring electric-field plasma waves, electron plasma frequency/density, and wave-particle activity in planetary magnetospheres and the heliosphere from 10 Hz to 56 kHz, using the shared 10-m electric antennas of the planetary radio astronomy investigation

Voyager LECP (Low-Energy Charged Particles) energetic-particle instrument measuring electrons, protons, alpha particles, and heavy ions in planetary magnetospheres and the heliosphere; comprising LEPT (Low-Energy Particle Telescope) and LEMPA (Low-Energy Magnetospheric Particle Analyzer), with 8-sector 360° scans and coverage of ~10 keV to >11 MeV electrons, ~15 keV to ≥150 MeV ions, and Z=3-26 nuclei (~0.05-30 MeV/nucleon)

Voyager 2 LECP (Low-Energy Charged Particles) energetic particle instrument measuring directional electrons (~10 keV to >11 MeV) and ions/protons/heavy nuclei (~15 keV to ≥150 MeV; composition Z=1–26 over ~0.05–30 MeV) in interplanetary and planetary environments, comprising the LEPT (Low-Energy Particle Telescope) and LEMPA (Low-Energy Magnetospheric Particle Analyzer) scanning through eight 45° sectors

Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 MAG (Magnetometer) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer investigation measuring vector magnetic fields in the solar wind, at Jupiter and Saturn, and through the outer heliosphere/heliosheath; uses low-field and high-field sensors with interplanetary accuracy ~0.1 nT and dynamic range ~0.01 nT to 2×10^-3 T

Voyager 1 Ephemeris spacecraft trajectory and position data product providing time-tagged Voyager 1 location, range, and velocity coordinates for heliospheric context, used to relate plasma, fields, energetic-particle, and radio measurements to spacecraft position along the outbound trajectory through the outer heliosphere and interstellar medium

Voyager 1/Voyager 2 PLS (Plasma Science) Faraday-cup plasma spectrometer measuring solar-wind and planetary-magnetospheric ion/electron distributions, bulk speed, density, temperature and pressure; comprising three coaxial Earth-pointing ion cups A, B and C and a side-looking cup D, with stepped E/q scans from ~10 eV/q to 6 keV/q and side-cup electrons ~5 eV-1 keV

Voyager CRS (Cosmic Ray System) energetic-particle telescope suite measuring cosmic-ray and planetary energetic-particle spectra, composition, and anisotropies; comprising HETS (High-Energy Telescope System; Z=1-30 nuclei ~6-500 MeV/nucleon and electrons ~3-100 MeV) and LETS (Low-Energy Telescope System; Z=1-30 nuclei ~0.15-30 MeV/nucleon), including electron telescope measurements of MeV electrons

Voyager 2 MAG (Magnetic Fields Investigation) triaxial fluxgate magnetometer instrument measuring vector magnetic fields in the solar wind and the magnetospheres of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune; uses two low-field and two high-field triaxial fluxgate sensors spanning ~0.01 nT to 2×10^-3 T with ~0.1 nT interplanetary-field accuracy

Voyager 2 PLS (Plasma Spectrometer) Faraday-cup plasma instrument measuring solar-wind and planetary-magnetospheric ion/electron distributions, bulk velocity, density, temperature and pressure; uses four modulated-grid Faraday cups—three earthward-facing ion cups and one side-looking electron cup—with sequential energy scans and electron coverage ~5 eV-1 keV

Wind 3DP (Three-Dimensional Plasma and Energetic Particle) particle spectrometer suite measuring 3D electron and ion distributions, moments, pitch-angle distributions, and suprathermal/energetic particles from ~10 eV to ~5 MeV; comprising EESA-L/EESA-H (Electron Electrostatic Analyzer low/high), PESA-L/PESA-H (Proton Electrostatic Analyzer low/high), and SST Foil/Open (Solid State Telescope) sensors

Wind EPACT (Energetic Particle Acceleration, Composition and Transport) energetic-particle suite measuring suprathermal/energetic ions/electrons, solar energetic particles, anomalous/galactic cosmic rays, protons, He, and heavy-ion elemental/isotopic composition (~20 keV/n to ~500 MeV/n; Z to U) for acceleration/composition/transport studies; comprising STEP (Suprathermal Energetic Particle Telescope), LEMT (Low-Energy Matrix Telescope), APE (Alpha Proton Electron), and IT (Isotope Telescope)

Wind WAVES (Plasma and Radio Waves) waveform receiver and radio/plasma wave investigation measuring electric and magnetic field waves and solar radio emissions from sub-Hz to ~14 MHz; comprising RAD1, RAD2, TNR (Thermal Noise Receiver), TDS (Time Domain Sampler), FFT/waveform and fast-envelope channels fed by spin-plane/axial electric antennas and a triaxial search coil

Wind STICS (SupraThermal Ion Composition Spectrometer) energetic-particle time-of-flight mass spectrometer measuring suprathermal ion energy, mass, mass/charge, charge-state/composition, and angular distributions from ~6-230 keV/e; one of the three SMS (Solar Wind and Suprathermal Ion Composition) suite sensors alongside SWICS and MASS.

Wind SWICS (Solar Wind Ion Composition Spectrometer) solar-wind ion composition spectrometer measuring ion energy, mass, mass-per-charge, charge states, elemental and isotopic composition from ~0.5-30 keV/e; one of the three SMS (Solar Wind and Suprathermal Ion Composition) suite sensors alongside MASS (Mass Time-of-Flight Spectrometer) and STICS (Suprathermal Ion Composition Spectrometer)
